bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 123卷 卷第一百二十三 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, Volume 123, Scroll the One Hundred and Twenty-Third.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 123.

sentences.zh: 【宋紀五】 起柔兆困敦，盡重光大荒落，凡六年。。

translations.literal: [Song Records, Part Five]—beginning at Rouzhao-Kundun and ending at Chongguang-Dahuangluo, six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 5], from the bingzi year-name cycle through the dinghai year-name cycle—a span of six years.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之上元嘉十三年（丙子，公元四三六年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 13 (bingzi; AD 436).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 13 of Emperor Wen's reign (bingzi; AD 436).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑朔，上有疾，不朝會。。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day guichou, the emperor was ill and did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on New Year's Day (guichou), the emperor was ill and held no court audience.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏主還宮。。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Wei emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Northern Wei emperor returned to his capital.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊子，燕王遣使入貢於魏，請送侍子，魏主不許，將舉兵討之，壬辰，遣使才十餘輩詣東方高麗等諸國告諭之。。

translations.literal: Second month, on wuzi, the King of Yan sent envoys to offer tribute to Wei and requested to send a hostage prince; the Wei emperor refused and prepared to raise troops to punish him. On renchen he dispatched barely more than ten envoys to the eastern states, including Koguryŏ, to announce and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuzi, the Yan king sent envoys to Wei with tribute and asked to send a hostage prince; the Wei emperor refused and prepared a punitive campaign. On renchen he sent a little over a dozen envoys to the eastern states, including Koguryŏ, to proclaim his intentions.

sentences.zh: 司空、江州刺史、永修公檀道濟，立功前朝，威名甚重，左右腹心並經百戰，諸子又有才氣，朝廷疑畏之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Inspector of Jiang Province, and Duke of Yongxiu Tan Daoji had rendered great service under the previous reign; his renown was very great, his close confidants had all fought through a hundred battles, and his sons were talented as well—the court both suspected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji, Minister of Works, inspector of Jiang Province, and Duke of Yongxiu, had won distinction under the previous emperor. His fame was immense, his inner circle were all veterans of countless campaigns, and his sons were gifted as well—the court viewed him with suspicion and dread.

sentences.zh: 帝久疾不愈，劉湛說司徒義康，以為：「宮車一日晏駕，道濟不復可制。」

translations.literal: The emperor's long illness did not improve. Liu Zhan persuaded the Minister of Works Liu Yikang, saying: "If the imperial carriage should one day pass in the evening, Tan Daoji will no longer be controllable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness dragged on without recovery. Liu Zhan urged the chief minister Liu Yikang, arguing: "Once the emperor passes away, Tan Daoji will be beyond anyone's control."

sentences.zh: 會帝疾篤，義康言於帝，召道濟入朝。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor's illness grew critical; Yikang spoke to the emperor and summoned Daoji to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's condition turned grave, Yikang persuaded him to summon Daoji to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其妻向氏謂道濟曰：「高世之勳，自古所忌。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Xiang, said to Daoji: "Merit that towers above the age has been envied since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Xiang, warned Daoji: "Supreme merit has always aroused jealousy.

sentences.zh: 今無事相召，禍其至矣。」

translations.literal: Now you are summoned when there is no business—disaster is surely at hand."
translations.idiomatic: To be summoned for no apparent reason—disaster must be near."

sentences.zh: 既至，留之累月。

translations.literal: After he arrived, they detained him for many months.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, they kept him at court for many months.

sentences.zh: 帝稍間，將遣還，已下渚，未發；

translations.literal: When the emperor improved slightly, they were about to send him back; he had already gone down to the ferry landing but had not yet departed;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rallied somewhat, the court prepared to send him home; he had reached the river landing but had not yet set out;

sentences.zh: 會帝疾動，義康矯詔召道濟入祖道，因執之。

translations.literal: then the emperor's illness relapsed; Yikang forged an edict summoning Daoji to a farewell feast and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's illness worsened again. Yikang forged an edict summoning Daoji to a parting banquet and had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 三月，己未，下詔稱：「道濟潛散金貨，招誘剽猾，因朕寢疾，規肆禍心。」

translations.literal: Third month, on jiwei, an edict was issued stating: "Tan Daoji has secretly dispersed gold and goods, recruited and enticed ruffians, and, taking advantage of Our illness in bed, plotted to unleash calamity."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiwei, an edict accused Tan Daoji of secretly distributing gold, recruiting outlaws, and exploiting the emperor's illness to hatch a treasonous plot."

sentences.zh: 收付廷尉，並其子給事黃門侍郎植等十一人誅之，唯宥其孫孺。

translations.literal: He was handed over to the Minister of Justice, and together with his sons—including Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zhi—and eleven others in all were executed; only his grandson Ru was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He was turned over to the judiciary; he and eleven others, including his son Zhi, attendant at the Yellow Gate, were put to death. Only his grandson Ru was spared.

sentences.zh: 又殺司空參軍薛彤、高進之。

translations.literal: They also killed the Minister of Works' staff officers Xue Tong and Gao Jinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The court also executed Xue Tong and Gao Jinzhi, staff officers on Daoji's staff.

sentences.zh: 二人皆道濟腹心，有勇力，時人比之關、張。。

translations.literal: Both were Daoji's trusted intimates, brave and strong; people of the time compared them to Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Both were Daoji's closest confidants, famed for their valor; contemporaries likened them to Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.

sentences.zh: 道濟見收，憤怒，目光如炬，脫幘投地曰：「乃壞汝萬里長城！」

translations.literal: When Daoji was taken, in anger his gaze blazed like torches; he tore off his headcloth and flung it to the ground, saying: "You are destroying your own ten-thousand-li Great Wall!"
translations.idiomatic: As Daoji was seized, his eyes blazed with fury; he tore off his cap and hurled it down, crying: "So you are tearing down your own Great Wall!"

sentences.zh: 魏人聞之，喜曰：「道濟死，吳子輩不足復憚！」。

translations.literal: When the people of Wei heard this, they rejoiced and said: "With Daoji dead, fellows like the men of Wu are no longer worth fearing!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei heard the news, they rejoiced: "With Daoji dead, the Wu generals are no longer worth fearing!"

sentences.zh: 庚申，大赦；

translations.literal: On gengshen, a general amnesty was proclaimed;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the court proclaimed a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍南譙王義宣為江州刺史。。

translations.literal: the General of the Central Army, Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao, general of the central army, inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏平東將軍娥清、安西將軍古弼將精騎一萬伐燕，平州刺史拓跋嬰帥遼西諸軍會之。。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Wei's Pacifier of the East E Qing and Pacifier of the West Gu Bi led ten thousand elite horsemen to attack Yan; Ping Province Inspector Tuoba Ying commanded the Liaoxi armies to join them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Wei generals E Qing and Gu Bi led ten thousand elite cavalry against Yan, while Ping Province inspector Tuoba Ying marched the Liaoxi forces to rendezvous with them.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊難當自稱大秦王，改元建義，立妻為王后，世子為太子，置百官皆如天子之制，然猶貢奉宋、魏不絕。。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Nandang styled himself Great King of Qin, changed the era name to Jianyi, installed his wife as queen and his heir as crown prince, and established the full bureaucracy in the manner of the Son of Heaven—yet he still sent tribute to Song and Wei without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Nandang proclaimed himself Great King of Qin, adopted the era name Jianyi, enthroned his wife as queen and his heir as crown prince, and set up a full court mirroring the imperial model—yet he continued sending tribute to both Song and Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏娥清、古弼攻燕白狼城，克之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Wei's E Qing and Gu Bi attacked Yan's city of Bailang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, E Qing and Gu Bi stormed Yan's city of Bailang and captured it.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣其將葛盧孟光將眾數萬隨陽伊至和龍迎燕王。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ sent its general Gelu Mengguang with tens of thousands of men, following Yang Yi to Helong to welcome the King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ dispatched General Gelu Mengguang with tens of thousands of troops; following Yang Yi, they marched to Helong to escort the Yan king.

sentences.zh: 高麗屯於臨川。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ encamped at Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Koguryŏ army encamped at Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 燕尚書令郭生因民之憚遷，開城門納魏兵；

translations.literal: Yan's Minister of the Masters of Writing Guo Sheng, because the people feared relocation, opened the city gates to admit Wei troops;
translations.idiomatic: Yan's chief minister Guo Sheng, exploiting popular dread of forced migration, opened the gates to Wei forces;

sentences.zh: 魏人疑之，不入。

translations.literal: the Wei troops suspected a trap and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: but the Wei troops suspected a trap and held back.

sentences.zh: 生遂勒兵攻燕王，王引高麗兵入自東門，與生戰於闕下，生中流矢死。

translations.literal: Sheng then led troops to attack the Yan king; the king brought Koguryŏ forces in through the east gate and fought Sheng below the gate-towers; Sheng was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then turned his troops against the Yan king, who brought Koguryŏ forces in through the east gate and fought him before the palace gates; Sheng fell to a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 葛盧孟光入城，命軍士脫弊褐，取燕武庫精仗以給之，大掠城中。。

translations.literal: Gelu Mengguang entered the city, ordered the soldiers to cast off their worn tunics, took fine arms from Yan's arsenal to equip them, and plundered the city on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Gelu Mengguang entered the city, had his men strip off their ragged clothes, armed them from Yan's arsenal, and looted the city thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙卯，燕王帥龍城見戶東徙，焚宮殿，火一旬不滅；

translations.literal: Fifth month, on yimao, the Yan king led the visible households of Longcheng eastward in migration, burned the palaces, and the fire did not die out for ten days;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yimao, the Yan king led Longcheng's populace eastward in exodus, torched the palaces, and the flames burned for ten days;

sentences.zh: 令婦人被甲居中，陽伊等勒精兵居外，葛盧孟光帥騎殿後，方軌而進，前後八十餘里。

translations.literal: he had women don armor and placed them in the center; Yang Yi and others led elite troops on the outside; Gelu Mengguang commanded cavalry as rearguard; they advanced in ordered ranks, the column stretching more than eighty li front to rear.
translations.idiomatic: women were armored and placed at the center of the column, Yang Yi and others led crack troops on the flanks, Gelu Mengguang commanded the cavalry rearguard, and the procession marched in tight formation for more than eighty li.

sentences.zh: 古弼部將高苟子帥騎欲追之，弼醉，拔刀止之，故燕王得逃去。

translations.literal: Gu Bi's subordinate Gao Gouzi led cavalry intending to pursue; Bi was drunk, drew his sword, and stopped him—thus the Yan king was able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bi's officer Gao Gouzi wanted to pursue with cavalry, but Bi, drunk, drew his sword and forbade it—allowing the Yan king to escape.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞之，怒，檻車征弼及娥清至平城，皆黜為門卒。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor heard of this, he was furious and summoned Bi and E Qing to Pingcheng in caged carts; both were demoted to gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor, enraged, had Bi and E Qing brought to Pingcheng in prisoner carts and reduced both to gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏主遣散騎常侍封撥使高麗，令送燕王。。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Wei emperor sent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Feng Bo as envoy to Koguryŏ, ordering them to hand over the King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Wei emperor sent attendant Feng Bo to Koguryŏ with orders to deliver the Yan king.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏主如河西。。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Wei emperor went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the Wei emperor traveled to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔寧朔將軍蕭汪之將兵討程道養。

translations.literal: Sixth month: an edict ordered General Who Pacifies the North Xiao Wangzhi to lead troops against Cheng Daoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the court ordered General Xiao Wangzhi to campaign against the rebel Cheng Daoyang.

sentences.zh: 軍至郪口，帛氐奴請降。

translations.literal: When the army reached Qikou, Bo Dinu requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Qikou, the rebel Bo Dinu offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 道養兵敗，還入郪山。。

translations.literal: Daoyang's army was defeated and withdrew into Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyang was defeated and fled back into the Qishan hills.

sentences.zh: 赫連定之西遷也，楊難當遂據上邽。

translations.literal: When Helian Ding moved west, Yang Nandang thereupon seized Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After Helian Ding withdrew westward, Yang Nandang seized Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏主遣驃騎大將軍樂平王丕、尚書令劉絜督河西、高平諸軍以討之，先遣平東將軍崔賾繼詔書諭難當。。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the Wei emperor sent Grand General of Agile Cavalry the Prince of Leping Pi and Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie to supervise the Hexi and Gaoping armies in punishing him; he first dispatched Pacifier of the East Cui Lin with an edict to instruct Nandang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Wei emperor sent Prince Pi of Leping and Liu Jie to command the Hexi and Gaoping armies against him, first dispatching Cui Lin with an imperial edict summoning Nandang to submit.

sentences.zh: 魏散騎侍郎游雅來聘。。

translations.literal: Wei's Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry You Ya came on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya of Wei arrived as envoy on a diplomatic mission to Song.

sentences.zh: 己未，零陵王太妃褚氏卒，追謚曰晉恭思皇后，葬以晉禮。。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Princess Dowager of the Prince of Lingling, Lady Chu, died; she was posthumously ennobled as Empress Gongsi of Jin and buried according to Jin rites.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Lady Chu, mother of the Prince of Lingling, died; she was posthumously honored as Empress Gongsi of Jin and interred with Jin ceremonial rites.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏主畋於河西。。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the Wei emperor hunted in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Wei emperor hunted in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣廣平公張黎發定州兵一萬二千通莎泉道。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent the Duke of Guangping Zhang Li to mobilize twelve thousand troops from Ding Province to open the Shaqüan route.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Duke Zhang Li of Guangping to raise twelve thousand Ding Province troops to clear the Shaqüan road.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚戌，魏樂平王丕等至略陽；

translations.literal: Ninth month, on gengxu, Wei's Prince of Leping Pi and others reached Lueyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengxu, Prince Pi of Leping and the Wei host reached Lueyang;

sentences.zh: 楊難當懼，請奉詔，攝上邽守兵還仇池。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang was afraid and asked to obey the edict, gathering the garrison troops of Shanggui and returning to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang, alarmed, submitted to the edict, withdrew the Shanggui garrison, and returned to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 諸將議，以為：「不誅其豪帥，軍還之後，必相聚為亂。

translations.literal: The generals deliberated, holding that: "If we do not execute their powerful chieftains, after the army withdraws they will surely gather and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The generals debated, arguing: "Unless we execute their chieftains, they will rally in rebellion once we withdraw.

sentences.zh: 又，大眾遠出，不有所掠，無以充軍實，賞將士。」

translations.literal: Moreover, with a great host far from home, if we take no plunder we have no means to fill the army's stores and reward the officers and men."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, an army this far from home must seize booty to fill its stores and reward the troops."

sentences.zh: 丕將從之，中書侍郎高允參丕軍事，諫曰：「如諸將之謀，是傷其向化之心；

translations.literal: Pi was about to agree; Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun served on Pi's staff and remonstrated, saying: "As the generals propose, this would wound their hearts that incline toward transformation;
translations.idiomatic: Pi was ready to agree, but Gao Yun, on his staff, objected: "To follow the generals' plan would destroy the goodwill of those who have submitted;

sentences.zh: 大軍既還，為亂必速。」

translations.literal: once the great army has returned, rebellion will come swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: once our army withdraws, rebellion will follow at once."

sentences.zh: 丕乃止，撫慰初附，秋毫不犯，秦、隴遂安。

translations.literal: Pi then desisted, comforted those newly submitted, and did not violate so much as an autumn hair—Qin and Long were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Pi relented, reassured the newly submitted peoples, and forbade the slightest pillage; Qin and Long were soon at peace.

sentences.zh: 難當以其子順為雍州刺史，守下辨。

translations.literal: Nandang appointed his son Shun Inspector of Yong Province to guard Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang installed his son Shun as inspector of Yong Province to hold Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 高麗不送燕王於魏，遣使奉表，稱「當與馮弘俱奉王化」。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ did not deliver the King of Yan to Wei but sent envoys with a memorial stating that they "would together with Feng Hong submit to royal transformation."
translations.idiomatic: “Koguryŏ refused to hand the Yan king to Wei and sent envoys pledging that they and Feng Hong would both accept Wei's overlordship.”

sentences.zh: 魏主以高麗違詔，議擊之，將發隴右騎卒。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, because Koguryŏ had defied the edict, debated attacking them and was about to mobilize the cavalry of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by Koguryŏ's defiance, the Wei emperor debated an attack and prepared to mobilize the Longyou cavalry.

sentences.zh: 劉絜曰：「秦、隴新民，且當優復，俟其饒實，然後用之。」

translations.literal: Liu Jie said: "The new subjects of Qin and Long should first be given generous relief; wait until they are rich and substantial, and only then employ them."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie urged: "The newly pacified peoples of Qin and Long need time to recover; only when they are prosperous should we draw on them."

sentences.zh: 樂平王丕曰：「和龍新定，宜廣修農桑以豐軍實，然後進取，則高麗一舉可滅也。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Leping Pi said: "Helong has only lately been pacified; we should broadly promote agriculture and sericulture to enrich the army's stores, and only then advance—then Koguryŏ can be destroyed in a single stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pi of Leping added: "Helong was only recently secured; we should expand farming to fill our stores, then advance—Koguryŏ could be crushed in one campaign."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃止。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，封皇子浚為始興王，駿為武陵王。。

translations.literal: On guichou, the imperial sons Jun and Jun were enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing and Prince of Wuling respectively.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the princes Jun and Jun were enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing and Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己酉，魏主如稒陽，驅野馬於雲中，置野馬苑。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on jiyou: the Wei emperor went to Boyang, drove wild horses in Yunzhong, and established a Wild Horse Park.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiyou, the Wei emperor traveled to Boyang, rounded up wild horses in Yunzhong, and established a royal stud.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬子，還宮。。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on renzi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renzi, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖克長安，得古銅渾儀，儀狀雖舉，不綴七曜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Gaozu took Chang'an, he obtained an ancient bronze armillary sphere; though its form was complete, it did not track the seven luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Emperor Gaozu captured Chang'an, he acquired an ancient bronze armillary sphere; though intact in form, it could not track the seven luminaries.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔太史令錢樂之更鑄渾儀，逕六尺八分，以水轉之，昏明中星與天相應。。

translations.literal: This year an edict ordered Grand Astrologer Qian Yuezhi to recast the armillary sphere, six chi and eight fen in diameter, driven by water; the stars at dusk, dawn, and meridian passage corresponded with heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court ordered Grand Astrologer Qian Yuezhi to cast a new armillary sphere six chi eight fen across, water-driven so that the stars at dusk, dawn, and culmination matched the heavens.

sentences.zh: 柔然與魏絕和親，犯魏邊。。

translations.literal: Rouran broke off marriage alliance with Wei and raided Wei's borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran severed ties with Wei and raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 吐欲渾惠王慕瑰卒，弟慕利延立。。

translations.literal: Mugui, King Hui of the Tuyuhun, died; his younger brother Muli Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Mugui, the Tuyuhun king known as Hui, died; his brother Muli Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之上元嘉十四年（丁丑，公元四三七年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 14 (dingchou; AD 437).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 14 of Emperor Wen's reign (dingchou; AD 437).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子，魏北平宣王長孫嵩卒。。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on wuzi, Wei's Prince Xuan of Beiping, Changsun Song, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuzi, Changsun Song, Prince Xuan of Beiping under Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，大赦。。

translations.literal: On xinmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，魏主如幽州。

translations.literal: Second month, on yimao, the Wei emperor went to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao, the Wei emperor traveled to You Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，魏主以南平王渾為鎮東大將軍、儀同三司，鎮和龍。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingchou: the Wei emperor appointed the Prince of Nanping Hun Grand General Who Guards the East and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, to garrison Helong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingchou, the Wei emperor appointed Prince Hun of Nanping grand general guarding the east with third-rank honors to hold Helong.

sentences.zh: 己卯，還宮。。

translations.literal: On jimao, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝遣散騎常侍劉熙伯如魏議納幣，會帝女亡而止。。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Liu Xibo to Wei to discuss the presentation of betrothal gifts; when the emperor's daughter died, the mission was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Xibo to Wei to negotiate betrothal gifts, but the mission was called off when the emperor's daughter died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，趙廣、張尋、梁顯等各帥眾降。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Zhao Guang, Zhang Xun, Liang Xian, and others each led their followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhao Guang, Zhang Xun, Liang Xian, and others surrendered with their bands.

sentences.zh: 別將王道恩斬程道養，送首，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: The separate commander Wang Dao'en beheaded Cheng Daoyang, sent the head, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-commander Wang Dao'en killed Cheng Daoyang and sent his head; the remaining rebels were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以輔國將軍周籍之為益州刺史。。

translations.literal: On dingwei, General Who Supports the State Zhou Jizhi was appointed Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Zhou Jizhi, general who supports the state, was made inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 魏主以民官多貪，夏，五月，己丑，詔吏民得舉告守令不如法者。

translations.literal: Because many local officials were corrupt, the Wei emperor, in summer, fifth month, on jichou, ordered that officials and commoners might report prefects and magistrates who did not act according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Finding many local officials corrupt, the Wei emperor, in the fifth month of summer, on jichou, allowed officials and commoners to denounce lawless prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 於是奸猾專求牧宰之失，迫脅在位，橫於閭裡；

translations.literal: Thereupon the crafty and unscrupulous devoted themselves to finding the faults of regional administrators, coerced those in office, and ran rampant through the neighborhoods;
translations.idiomatic: Crafty men then hunted for officials' misdeeds, intimidated officeholders, and terrorized the neighborhoods;

sentences.zh: 而長吏鹹降心待之，貪縱如故。。

translations.literal: yet the senior officials all humbled their hearts before them, and greed and license continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: while senior officials humbled themselves before them and remained as greedy and lawless as ever.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏主如雲中。。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Wei emperor went to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the Wei emperor traveled to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊子，魏永昌王健等討山胡白龍餘黨於西河，滅之。。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on wuzi: Wei's Prince of Yongchang Jian and others campaigned against the remnant band of the Mountain Hu leader Bai Long in Xihe and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuzi, Prince Jian of Yongchang and others crushed the remnants of the Mountain Hu rebel Bai Long in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiachen, the Wei emperor went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiachen, the Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲申，還宮。。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jiashen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiashen, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，魏主遣使者拜吐谷渾王慕利延為鎮西大將軍、儀同三司，改封西平王。。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Wei emperor sent envoys to invest the Tuyuhun king Muli Yan as Grand General Who Guards the West and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, changing his enfeoffment to Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the Wei emperor invested Tuyuhun king Muli Yan as grand general guarding the west with third-rank honors and enfeoffed him as Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸卯，魏主如雲中。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on guimao, the Wei emperor went to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guimao, the Wei emperor traveled to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬申，還宮。。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renshen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 魏主復遣散騎侍郎董琬、高明等多繼金帛，使西域，招撫九國。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor again sent Gentlemen Attendants of the Scattered Cavalry Dong Wan, Gao Ming, and others with further gold and silks as envoys to the Western Regions to win over and pacify the nine states.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor again dispatched Dong Wan, Gao Ming, and others with more gold and silk to the Western Regions to win over the nine states.

sentences.zh: 琬等至烏孫，其王甚喜，曰：「破洛那、者舌二國皆欲稱臣致貢於魏，但無路自致耳，今使君宜過撫之。」

translations.literal: When Wan and the others reached Wusun, its king was greatly pleased and said: "The two states of Poluona and Zheshi both wish to submit and offer tribute to Wei, but have no road by which to present themselves; the envoy should now go and comfort them."
translations.idiomatic: At Wusun, its king welcomed them warmly, saying: "Poluona and Zheshi both wish to submit to Wei but lack a route; your lordship should visit and reassure them."

sentences.zh: 乃遣導譯送琬詣破落那，明詣者舌。

translations.literal: He then sent guides and interpreters to escort Wan to Poluona and Ming to Zheshi.
translations.idiomatic: He provided guides to escort Wan to Poluona and Ming to Zheshi.

sentences.zh: 帝國聞之，爭遣使者隨琬等入貢，凡十六國。

translations.literal: When the imperial states heard of this, they vied to send envoys following Wan and the others to offer tribute—sixteen states in all.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, sixteen states sent envoys with Wan's party to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲朝貢不絕。。

translations.literal: From this time forward, annual tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth they sent tribute every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 魏主以其妹武威公主妻河西王牧犍，河西王遣宋繇奉表詣平城謝，且問其母及公主所宜稱。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor gave his sister, the Princess of Wuwei, in marriage to the King of Hexi, Mujian; the King of Hexi sent Song Yao with a memorial to Pingcheng to give thanks and also to ask what titles his mother and the princess should bear.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor married his sister, Princess Wuwei, to Hexi king Mujian, who sent Song Yao to Pingcheng with thanks and to ask what titles his mother and the princess should use.

sentences.zh: 魏主使群臣議之，皆曰：「母以子貴，妻從夫爵。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor had the ministers discuss it; all said: "The mother is ennobled through the son; the wife follows her husband's rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor consulted his ministers, who ruled: "A mother is honored through her son; a wife takes her husband's rank.

sentences.zh: 牧犍母宜稱河西國太后，公主於其國稱王后，於京師則稱公主。」

translations.literal: Mujian's mother should be styled Empress Dowager of the State of Hexi; in that state the princess should be styled queen, and in the capital she should be styled princess."
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's mother should be Empress Dowager of Hexi; in Hexi the princess should be called queen, and in the capital, princess."

sentences.zh: 魏主從之。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，牧犍娶涼武昭王之女，及魏公主至，李氏與其母尹氏遷居酒泉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mujian had married a daughter of the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang; when the Wei princess arrived, Lady Li and her mother Lady Yin moved to live at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian had earlier married a daughter of the Liang king; when the Wei princess arrived, Lady Li and her mother Lady Yin were moved to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，李氏卒，尹氏撫之，不哭，曰：「汝國破家亡，今死晚矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Lady Li died; Lady Yin stroked the corpse without weeping and said: "Your state was destroyed and your family ruined—your death has come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lady Li died; Lady Yin caressed the body without tears, saying: "Your kingdom fell and your house was ruined—you died too late."

sentences.zh: 牧犍之弟無諱鎮酒泉，謂尹氏曰：「後諸孫在伊吾，後欲就之乎？」

translations.literal: Mujian's younger brother Wuhui garrisoned Jiuquan and said to Lady Yin: "Your grandsons are at Yiwu—would you later wish to join them?"
translations.idiomatic: Mujian's brother Wuhui, holding Jiuquan, asked Lady Yin: "Your grandsons are at Yiwu—do you wish to join them someday?"

sentences.zh: 尹氏未測其意，紿之曰：「吾子孫漂蕩，托身異域，餘生無幾，當死此，不復為氈裘之鬼也。」

translations.literal: Lady Yin could not fathom his intent and deceived him, saying: "My descendants drift in exile, trusting their bodies to foreign lands; my remaining years are few—I shall die here and not become a ghost in felt and fur again."
translations.idiomatic: Unsure of his intent, she feigned agreement: "My kin wander in exile; I have few years left and will die here rather than end as a nomad ghost."

sentences.zh: 未幾，潛奔伊吾。

translations.literal: Before long she secretly fled to Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she secretly fled to Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 無諱遣騎追及之，尹氏謂追騎曰：「沮渠酒泉許吾歸北，何為復追！

translations.literal: Wuhui sent horsemen in pursuit and overtook her; Lady Yin said to the pursuers: "The Juqu of Jiuquan promised I might return north—why pursue me again!
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui sent cavalry after her; Lady Yin told them: "The Juqu of Jiuquan promised I could go north—why chase me again!

sentences.zh: 汝取吾首以往，吾不復還矣。」

translations.literal: Take my head and go—I shall not return."
translations.idiomatic: Take my head and go—I will not turn back."

sentences.zh: 追騎不敢逼，引還。

translations.literal: The pursuers dared not press her and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The horsemen dared not force her and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尹氏卒於伊吾。。

translations.literal: Lady Yin died at Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin died at Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 牧犍遣將軍沮渠旁周入貢於魏，魏主遣侍中古弼、尚書李順賜其侍臣衣服，並征世子封壇入侍。

translations.literal: Mujian sent the general Juqu Pangzhou to offer tribute to Wei; the Wei emperor sent Palace Attendant Gu Bi and Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Shun to bestow garments on his attending ministers, and also summoned the heir Fengtan to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian sent General Juqu Pangzhou to Wei with tribute; the Wei emperor sent Gu Bi and Li Shun with robes for his courtiers and summoned the heir Fengtan to attend court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，牧犍遣封壇如魏，亦遣使詣建康，獻雜書及敦煌趙𢾺所撰《甲寅元歷》，並求雜書數十種，帝皆與之。

translations.literal: That year Mujian sent Fengtan to Wei and also sent envoys to Jiankang, presenting miscellaneous books and the Jiayin Origin Calendar composed by Zhao 𢾺 of Dunhuang, and requesting several dozen other works; the emperor gave him all of them.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mujian sent Fengtan to Wei and envoys to Jiankang with books, including Zhao 𢾺 of Dunhuang's Jiayin Origin Calendar, and requested dozens of other works; the Song emperor granted them all.

sentences.zh: 李順自河西還，魏主問之曰：「卿往年言取涼州之策，朕以東方有事，未遑也。

translations.literal: When Li Shun returned from Hexi, the Wei emperor asked him: "You spoke in former years of the plan to take Liang Province; We had business in the east and had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun returned from Hexi, the Wei emperor asked: "Years ago you urged taking Liangzhou; eastern affairs kept me from acting.

sentences.zh: 今和龍己平，吾欲即以此年西征，可乎？」

translations.literal: Now Helong is already pacified—We wish to launch the western campaign this very year. Is it feasible?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Helong is pacified—may I campaign west this year?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣疇昔所言，以今觀之，私謂不謬。

translations.literal: He replied: "What your servant said in former days, viewed in the present, I privately consider not mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "What I said then still holds, in my view.

sentences.zh: 然國家戎車屢動，士馬疲勞，西征之義，請俟它年。」

translations.literal: Yet the state's war-chariots have moved repeatedly; soldiers and horses are weary—the western campaign, I beg, should await another year."
translations.idiomatic: But the army has campaigned repeatedly; men and horses are exhausted—please defer the western campaign to another year."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃止。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之上元嘉十五年（戊寅，公元四三八年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 15 (wuyin; AD 438).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 15 of Emperor Wen's reign (wuyin; AD 438).

sentences.zh: 春，二月，丁未，以吐谷渾王慕利延為都督西秦、河、沙三州諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、西秦、河二州刺史、隴西王。。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, on dingwei: the Tuyuhun king Muli Yan was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General Who Guards the West, Inspector of the two provinces of Western Qin and He, and Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on dingwei, Tuyuhun king Muli Yan was appointed commander of Western Qin, He, and Sha, grand general guarding the west, inspector of Western Qin and He, and Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸未，魏主詔罷沙門年五十已下者。。

translations.literal: Third month, on guiwei: the Wei emperor ordered that Buddhist monks under fifty years of age be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guiwei, the Wei emperor ordered monks under fifty to leave the clergy.

sentences.zh: 初，燕王弘至遼東，高麗王璉遣使勞之曰：「龍城王馮君，愛適野次，士馬勞乎？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Yan king Hong reached Liaodong, the Koguryŏ king Jian sent envoys to comfort him, saying: "King Feng of Longcheng, having halted in the wilds on your journey—are your men and horses weary?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan king Hong reached Liaodong, Koguryŏ king Jian sent envoys asking: "King Feng of Longcheng, resting in the wild on your journey—are your men and horses weary?"

sentences.zh: 弘慚怒，稱制讓之。

translations.literal: Hong, ashamed and angry, assumed imperial style and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, shamed and furious, styled himself emperor and rebuked Jian.

sentences.zh: 高麗處之平郭，尋徙北豐。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ lodged him at Pingguo, then soon moved him to Beifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ housed him at Pingguo, then moved him to Beifeng.

sentences.zh: 弘素侮高麗，政刑賞罰，猶如其國。

translations.literal: Hong had always looked down on Koguryŏ; in government, punishments, rewards, and penalties he still acted as in his own state.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had always despised Koguryŏ and continued to govern, punish, and reward as if still in Yan.

sentences.zh: 高麗乃奪其侍人，取其太子王仁為質。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ thereupon seized his attendants and took his crown prince Wang Ren as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ seized his attendants and took his heir Wang Ren hostage.

sentences.zh: 弘怨高麗，遣使來上表求迎，上遣使者王白駒等迎之，並令高麗資遣。

translations.literal: Hong resented Koguryŏ and sent envoys with a memorial requesting escort south; the emperor sent the envoy Wang Baiju and others to welcome him and also ordered Koguryŏ to supply provisions for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, resenting Koguryŏ, petitioned Song for escort; the emperor sent Wang Baiju and others to fetch him and ordered Koguryŏ to provide supplies.

sentences.zh: 高麗王不欲使弘南來，遣將孫漱、高仇等殺弘於北豐，並其子孫十餘人，謚弘曰昭成皇帝。

translations.literal: The Koguryŏ king did not wish Hong to come south and sent the generals Sun Shu and Gao Chou and others to kill Hong at Beifeng, together with more than ten of his sons and grandsons; he gave Hong the posthumous title Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to let Hong go south, the Koguryŏ king sent Sun Shu and Gao Chou to kill him at Beifeng with more than ten kin and posthumously styled him Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 白駒等帥所領七千餘人掩討漱、仇，殺仇，生擒漱。

translations.literal: Baiju and others led their more than seven thousand men in a surprise attack on Shu and Chou, killed Chou, and captured Shu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Baiju led his seven thousand men in a surprise raid, killed Chou, and captured Shu alive.

sentences.zh: 高麗王以白駒等專殺，遣使執送之。

translations.literal: The Koguryŏ king, because Baiju and the others had killed on their own authority, sent envoys to seize and deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: The Koguryŏ king protested their unauthorized killings and sent envoys to seize and deliver them to Song.

sentences.zh: 上以遠國，不欲違其意，下白駒等獄；

translations.literal: Because it was a distant state, the emperor did not wish to go against their wishes and imprisoned Baiju and the others;
translations.idiomatic: Not wishing to offend a distant ally, the emperor imprisoned Baiju and his men;

sentences.zh: 已而原之。。

translations.literal: but afterward pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: then later pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，納故黃門侍郎殷淳女為太子劭妃。。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the daughter of the late Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate Yin Chun was taken in marriage as consort to the crown prince Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the daughter of the late Yin Chun was wed to Crown Prince Shao.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊寅，魏大赦。。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on wuyin: Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuyin, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏主如五原。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Wei emperor went to Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the Wei emperor went to Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，自五原北伐柔然。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: from Wuyuan he marched north to attack the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, he marched north from Wuyuan against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 命樂平王丕督十五將出東道，永昌王健督十五將出西道，魏主自出中道。

translations.literal: He ordered the Prince of Leping Pi to supervise fifteen generals on the eastern route, Prince Jian of Yongchang to supervise fifteen generals on the western route, and the Wei emperor himself to take the central route.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pi of Leping led fifteen generals on the eastern route, Prince Jian of Yongchang fifteen on the western route, and the emperor took the center.

sentences.zh: 至浚稽山，復分中道為二：陳留王崇從大澤向涿邪山，魏主從浚稽北向天山，西登白阜，不見柔然而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Mount Junji, he again divided the central route in two: the Prince of Chenliu Chong went from the Great Marsh toward Mount Zhuoye; the Wei emperor went north from Junji toward Mount Tianshan, ascended Bai Fu in the west, saw no Rouran, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Junji he split the center: Prince Chong of Chenliu marched from the Great Marsh toward Zhuoye Mountain while the emperor went north toward Tianshan, climbed Bai Fu, found no Rouran, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 時漠北大旱，無水草，人馬多死。

translations.literal: At that time the northern desert suffered great drought; there was no water or grass, and many men and horses died.
translations.idiomatic: The northern steppe was gripped by drought; lacking water and fodder, many men and horses perished.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丁卯朔，日有食之。。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on the first day dingmao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on New Year's Day (dingmao), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁巳，魏主至平城。。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on dingsi, the Wei emperor reached Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 豫章雷次宗好學，隱居廬山。

translations.literal: Lei Cizong of Yuzhang loved learning and lived in seclusion on Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Cizong of Yuzhang, a devoted scholar, lived in seclusion on Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 嘗征為散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: He was once summoned as Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Once summoned as scattered-cavalry attendant, he declined.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以處士征至建康，為開館於雞籠山，使聚徒教授。

translations.literal: This year he was summoned as a recluse to Jiankang; a hall was opened for him on Mount Jilong, and he was made to gather disciples and teach.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was summoned to Jiankang as a recluse; a school was opened for him on Mount Jilong to gather and instruct students.

sentences.zh: 帝雅好藝文，使丹陽尹廬江何尚之立玄學，太子率更令何承天立史學，司徒參軍謝元立文學，並次宗儒學為四學。

translations.literal: The emperor was fond of arts and letters and had the Governor of Danyang He Shangzhi of Lujiang establish the study of arcane learning, the crown prince's Director of Waterways He Chengtian establish the study of history, and the staff officer of the Minister of Works Xie Yuan establish the study of belles lettres—together with Cizong's study of Confucian learning, these were the Four Studies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, devoted to culture, had He Shangzhi head metaphysics, He Chengtian history, Xie Yuan literature, and Lei Cizong Confucian studies—the Four Academies.

sentences.zh: 元，靈運之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Yuan was a younger cousin of Xie Lingyun on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yuan was a cousin of the poet Xie Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 帝數幸次宗學館，令次宗以巾示冓侍講，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited Cizong's academy, had Cizong signal with a kerchief when it was time to lecture, and granted him very generous support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Cizong's school, had him signal lectures with a kerchief, and lavished gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 又除給事中，不就。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Supervising Secretary but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again offered the post of supervising secretary and again declined.

sentences.zh: 久之，還廬山。。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he returned to Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：《易》曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」

translations.literal: Your servant Guang remarks: The Book of Changes says: "The noble person widely knows the words and deeds of former ages to store up his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: The Book of Changes says, "The noble person learns widely from the words and deeds of the past to cultivate virtue."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「辭達而已矣。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Language that gets through—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Language need only convey the meaning—that is all."

sentences.zh: 然則史者儒之一端，文者儒之餘事；

translations.literal: Thus history is one branch of the Confucian way, and belles lettres are the Confucian's spare affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Thus history is one branch of Confucian learning and literature a secondary pursuit;

sentences.zh: 至於老、莊虛無，固非所以為教也。

translations.literal: as for the emptiness of Laozi and Zhuangzi, it is certainly not what should serve as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: while the emptiness of Laozi and Zhuangzi is no proper foundation for teaching.

sentences.zh: 夫學者所以求道；

translations.literal: Learning exists to seek the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship exists to seek the Way;

sentences.zh: 天下無二道，安有四學哉！。

translations.literal: under Heaven there are not two Ways—how can there be four studies!
translations.idiomatic: there is only one Way under Heaven—how can there be four separate schools!

sentences.zh: 帝性仁厚恭儉，勤於為政，守法而不峻，容物而不弛。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was benevolent, generous, respectful, and frugal; diligent in governing, he upheld the law without harshness and tolerated others without laxity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was benevolent, respectful, and frugal, diligent in government—strict in law yet not harsh, tolerant yet not lax.

sentences.zh: 百官皆久於其職，守宰以六期為斷，吏不苟免，民有所繫。

translations.literal: All officials long held their posts; prefects and magistrates were judged by six-year terms; clerks were not casually dismissed; the people had something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Officials served long in their posts; local leaders served fixed six-year terms; clerks were not dismissed capriciously; the people had stable governance to rely on.

sentences.zh: 三十年間，四境之內，晏安無事，戶口蕃息；

translations.literal: Within thirty years, throughout the four borders, there was peace and quiet without incident, and households and population flourished;
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years the realm within the four borders enjoyed peace and prosperity, and the population grew;

sentences.zh: 出租供徭，止於歲賦，晨出暮歸，自事而已。

translations.literal: For rent and corvée labor-service they paid only the annual levy; they went out at dawn and returned at dusk, attending to their own affairs—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée and rents were limited to the annual tax; people left at dawn and returned at dusk to mind their own work, and that was enough.

sentences.zh: 閭閻之內，講誦相聞；

translations.literal: Within the lanes and alleys, lecture and recitation could be heard from one another;
translations.idiomatic: In every neighborhood one could hear lectures and recitation;

sentences.zh: 士敦操尚，鄉恥輕薄。

translations.literal: gentlemen cultivated integrity and loftiness; hamlets shamed frivolity and license.
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen cultivated integrity; villages shamed frivolous conduct.

sentences.zh: 江左風俗，於斯為美。

translations.literal: The customs of the lands south of the Yangzi at this point were at their finest.
translations.idiomatic: South-of-the-Yangzi manners were at their best in this age.

sentences.zh: 後之言政治者，皆稱元嘉焉。。

translations.literal: Later speakers on government all praised the Yuanjia reign.
translations.idiomatic: Later commentators on governance all held up the Yuanjia era as a model.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之上元嘉十六年（己卯，公元四三九年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 16 (jimao; AD 439).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 16 (jimao; AD 439).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚寅，司徒義康進位大將軍、領司徒，南袞州刺史、江夏王義恭進位司空。。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on gengyin, Minister of Works Yikang was promoted to Grand General while retaining the ministership; the Inspector of Southern Guan and King of Jiangxia Yigong was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengyin, Yikang was promoted from Minister of Works to Grand General while keeping that office; Yigong, King of Jiangxia and inspector of Southern Guan, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏主如定州。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor went to Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor traveled to Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖遣詔，令諸子次第居荊州。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Founding Emperor left instructions that his sons should take turns residing in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu had decreed that his sons should rotate residence in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶在荊州八年，欲為之選代，其次應在南譙王義宣。

translations.literal: The King of Linchuan Yiqing had been in Jingzhou eight years; the court wished to select a replacement; by rotation it should have been the King of Nanqiao Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan had governed Jingzhou for eight years, and the court sought a successor; by rotation it should have been Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 帝以義宣人才凡鄙，置不用；

translations.literal: The emperor deemed Yixuan's talent altogether mean and vulgar and did not employ him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Yixuan's talent mean and vulgar and passed him over;

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，以衡陽王義季為都督荊、湘等八州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, on jihai, the King of Hengyang Yiji was made Area Commander-in-Chief of the eight provinces including Jing and Xiang, and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, Prince Yiji of Hengyang was appointed commander of military affairs in eight provinces including Jing and Xiang, and inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 義季嘗春月出畋，有老父被苫而耕，左右斥之，老父曰：「盤於游畋，古人所戒。

translations.literal: Yiji once went out hunting in spring; an old man wearing a straw cape was plowing—the attendants drove him off. The old man said: "Indulgence in roaming and hunting is what the ancients warned against.
translations.idiomatic: One spring Yiji went hunting. An old man in a straw cape was plowing; his attendants drove him away. The old man said, "Indulgence in roaming and hunting is what the ancients warned against.

sentences.zh: 今陽和布氣，一日不耕，民失其時，奈何以從禽之樂而驅斥老農也！」

translations.literal: Now the warm yang spreads its breath—miss one day's plowing and the people lose their season; how can you pursue the joy of hunting and drive off an old farmer!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the warm breath of spring is abroad—miss one day's plowing and the people lose their season. How can you chase birds for pleasure and drive off an old farmer!"

sentences.zh: 義季止馬曰：「賢者也！」

translations.literal: Yiji reined in his horse and said: "A worthy man!"
translations.idiomatic: Yiji reined in and said, "A worthy man!"

sentences.zh: 命賜之食，辭曰：「大王不奪農時，則境內之民皆飽大王之食，老夫何敢獨受大王之賜乎！」

translations.literal: He ordered food given him; the man declined: "If Your Highness does not steal the farming season, all the people within the borders will be sated on Your Highness's food—how dare this old man alone accept Your Highness's gift!"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered food brought, but the man declined: "If Your Highness does not steal the farming season, everyone in your realm will be fed by you—how dare this old man alone accept your gift!"

sentences.zh: 義季問其名，不告而退。。

translations.literal: Yiji asked his name; he would not tell it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji asked his name, but he would not say and left.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏雍州刺史葛那寇上洛，上洛太守鐔長生棄郡走。。

translations.literal: Third month: Wei's Inspector of Yong Gena raided Shangluo; Shangluo Administrator Tan Changsheng abandoned the commandery and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Gena, Northern Wei inspector of Yong, attacked Shangluo; Tan Changsheng, the prefect, abandoned the commandery and fled.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主還宮。。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Wei emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Northern Wei emperor returned to his capital.

sentences.zh: 楊保宗與兄保顯自童亭奔魏。

translations.literal: Yang Baozong and his elder brother Baoxian fled to Wei from Tongting.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Baozong and his elder brother Baoxian fled from Tongting to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主以保宗為都督隴西諸軍事、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、秦州牧、武都王，鎮上邽，妻以公主；

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Wei emperor made Baozong Area Commander-in-Chief of Longxi, Grand General Who Conquers the West, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Protocol to the Three Dukes, Governor of Qin Province, and King of Wudu, garrisoning Shanggui, and gave him a princess in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the Wei emperor made Baozong commander of Longxi, Grand General Who Conquers the West, with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes, governor of Qin, and King of Wudu, posted at Shanggui, and married him to a princess;

sentences.zh: 保顯為鎮西將軍、晉壽公。。

translations.literal: Baoxian was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxian was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 河西王牧犍通於其嫂李氏，兄弟三人傳嬖之。

translations.literal: The King of Hexi, Mujian, had relations with his sister-in-law Lady Li; the three brothers passed her among them in turn as a favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi king Mujian had an affair with his sister-in-law Lady Li, and the three brothers took turns keeping her as a favorite.

sentences.zh: 李氏與牧犍之姊共毒魏公主，魏主遣解毒醫乘傳救之，得愈。

translations.literal: Lady Li and Mujian's sister together poisoned the Wei princess; the Wei emperor sent an antidote physician by relay to save her, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li and Mujian's sister jointly poisoned the Wei princess; the Wei emperor sent an antidote physician by relay post, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 魏主征李氏，牧犍不遣，厚資給，使居酒泉。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor summoned Lady Li; Mujian would not send her but gave her rich support and had her live at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor demanded Lady Li, but Mujian refused to send her, gave her generous support, and settled her at Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 魏每遣使者詣西域，常詔牧犍發導護送出流沙。

translations.literal: Whenever Wei sent envoys to the Western Regions, it regularly ordered Mujian to dispatch guides and escorts to conduct them beyond the drifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wei sent envoys westward, it routinely ordered Mujian to provide guides and escorts to see them past the drifting sands.

sentences.zh: 使者自西域還，至武威，牧犍左右有告魏使者曰：「我君承蠕蠕可汗妄言云：『去歲魏天子自來伐我，士馬疫死，大敗而還；

translations.literal: When an envoy returned from the Western Regions and reached Wuwei, someone close to Mujian told the Wei envoy: "Our lord, following the Rouran khan's reckless talk, said: 'Last year the Wei Son of Heaven came in person to attack us; men and horses died of pestilence and he returned in great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: As an envoy returned from the west and reached Wuwei, someone near Mujian told the Wei envoy, "Our lord heard the Rouran khan's boast that 'last year the Wei emperor came in person to attack us; his men and horses died of plague and he fled in defeat;

sentences.zh: 我擒其長弟樂平王丕。』

translations.literal: we captured his eldest younger brother, the Prince of Leping, Pi.'
translations.idiomatic: we captured his younger brother, Prince Pi of Leping.'

sentences.zh: 我君大喜，宣言於國。

translations.literal: Our lord was greatly pleased and proclaimed it throughout the state.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord was delighted and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又聞可汗遣使告西域諸國，稱：『魏已削弱，今天下唯我為強，若更有魏使，勿復供奉。』

translations.literal: It was also heard that the khan sent envoys to tell the states of the Western Regions, saying: 'Wei is already weakened; now under Heaven only I am strong—if there should be another Wei envoy, do not again offer tribute.'
translations.idiomatic: We also heard that the khan told the western states, 'Wei is weakened; now only I am strong under Heaven—if another Wei envoy comes, do not receive him again.'

sentences.zh: 西域諸國頗有貳心。」

translations.literal: The states of the Western Regions largely harbored divided loyalties."
translations.idiomatic: Many western states began to waver in loyalty."

sentences.zh: 使還，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, he reported the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, the envoy reported all of this in detail.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣尚書賀多羅使涼州觀虛實，多羅還，亦言牧犍雖外修臣禮，內實乖悖。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Minister of the Masters of Writing He Duoluo to Liang Province to observe the true situation; when Duoluo returned, he too said that though Mujian outwardly observed the rites of a subject, inwardly he was in fact rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Minister He Duoluo to Liangzhou to reconnoiter; on his return Duoluo too said Mujian observed the forms of vassalage outwardly but was disloyal within.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲討之，以問崔浩。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor wished to campaign against him and asked Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wished to attack him and consulted Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「牧犍逆心已露，不可不誅。

translations.literal: He replied: "Mujian's rebellious intent is already exposed—he cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "Mujian's disloyalty is already plain; he must be punished.

sentences.zh: 官軍往年北伐，雖不克獲，實無所損。

translations.literal: The imperial army's northern campaign in past years, though it did not achieve capture, in truth suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's northern campaign, though it did not capture the enemy, did the state no real harm.

sentences.zh: 戰馬三十萬匹，計在道死傷不滿八千，常歲羸死亦不減萬匹。

translations.literal: Of three hundred thousand war-horses, those dead or wounded on the march amounted to fewer than eight thousand—an ordinary year's deaths from weakness would not be less than ten thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: Of three hundred thousand war-horses, fewer than eight thousand died or were wounded on the march—an ordinary year loses no fewer than ten thousand to weakness alone.

sentences.zh: 而遠方乘虛，遽謂衰耗不能復振。

translations.literal: Yet distant lands seized on the opening and hastily declared that exhaustion meant Wei could not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet distant lands seized the moment and declared that Wei was spent and could not recover.

sentences.zh: 今出其不意，大軍猝至，彼必駭擾，不知所為，擒之必矣。」

translations.literal: Now strike them unawares—when the great army suddenly arrives, they will surely be terrified and thrown into confusion, not knowing what to do; capture is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Strike now without warning; when the army suddenly arrives they will panic and not know what to do, and he will surely be taken."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「善！

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 吾意亦以為然。」

translations.literal: My mind too holds it so."
translations.idiomatic: I think so as well."

sentences.zh: 於是大集公卿議於西堂。。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly assembled the dukes and ministers to deliberate in the Western Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then convened the high ministers for deliberation in the Western Hall.

sentences.zh: 弘農王奚斤等三十餘人皆曰：「牧犍，西垂下國，雖心不純臣，然繼父位以來，職貢不乏。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hongnong Xi Jin and more than thirty others all said: "Mujian is a petty state on the western marches; though his heart is not that of a pure subject, yet since succeeding his father's position tribute and duties have not been lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi Jin of Hongnong and more than thirty others said, "Mujian is a minor western state; though not wholly loyal, since he succeeded his father he has not failed in tribute.

sentences.zh: 朝廷待以籓臣，妻以公主；

translations.literal: The court has treated him as a feudatory subject and given him a princess in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: The court has treated him as a vassal and married him to a princess;

sentences.zh: 今其罪惡未彰，宜加恕宥。

translations.literal: now his crimes and wickedness are not yet manifest—he should receive added forgiveness and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: his crimes are not yet proven; he should be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 國家新征蠕蠕，士馬疲弊，未可大舉。

translations.literal: The state has newly campaigned against the Rouran; men and horses are worn and depleted—a great expedition is not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: The state has just fought the Rouran; men and horses are exhausted—a major campaign is not yet possible.

sentences.zh: 且聞其土地鹵瘠，難得水草，大軍既至，彼必嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Moreover it is heard that their land is saline and barren, hard to obtain water and fodder; once the great army arrives, they will surely cling to their walls and hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their land is said to be saline and poor in water and grass; when the army arrives they will surely hold their walls.

sentences.zh: 攻之不拔，野無所掠，此危道也。」。

translations.literal: Attack without taking them, nothing to plunder in the wilds—this is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: If the siege fails and there is nothing to forage in the countryside, that is a dangerous path."

sentences.zh: 初，崔浩惡尚書李順，順使涼州凡十二返，魏主以為能。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Hao hated Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Shun; Shun had been envoy to Liang Province twelve times in all, and the Wei emperor considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Hao disliked Minister Li Shun, who had been envoy to Liangzhou twelve times and whom the emperor regarded as capable.

sentences.zh: 涼武宣王數與順游宴，對其群下時為驕慢之語；

translations.literal: The Martial and Illustrious King of Liang often feasted and toured with Shun, and before his subordinates at times uttered arrogant and contemptuous words;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang king often feasted with Shun and before his officials spoke arrogantly;

sentences.zh: 恐順洩之，隨以金寶納於順懷，順亦為之隱。

translations.literal: fearing Shun would leak them, he thereupon placed gold and jewels in Shun's bosom, and Shun too concealed the matter for him.
translations.idiomatic: fearing Shun would report this, he stuffed gold and jewels into Shun's robe, and Shun concealed it.

sentences.zh: 浩知之，密以白魏主，魏主未之信。

translations.literal: Hao knew it and secretly reported to the Wei emperor, but the Wei emperor did not yet believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao learned of this and secretly informed the emperor, who did not yet believe him.

sentences.zh: 及議伐涼州，順與尚書古弼皆曰：「自溫圉水以西至姑臧，地皆枯石，絕無水草。

translations.literal: When they deliberated on attacking Liang Province, Shun and Minister Gu Bi both said: "From the Wenyu River west to Guzang, the land is all withered stone, utterly without water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: When the attack on Liangzhou was debated, Shun and Minister Gu Bi both said, "From the Wenyu River west to Guzang the land is barren rock, utterly without water or grass.

sentences.zh: 彼人言，姑臧城南天梯山上，冬有積雪，深至丈餘，春夏消釋，下流成川，居民引以溉灌。

translations.literal: Those people say that south of Guzang on Mount Tianti snow accumulates in winter to more than a zhang in depth; in spring and summer it melts and flows down to form streams, which the inhabitants draw for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: They say that south of Guzang on Mount Tianti snow piles more than ten feet deep in winter; in spring and summer it melts into streams that the people use for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 彼聞軍至，決此渠口，水必乏絕。

translations.literal: When they hear the army has come, they will breach these channel mouths and water will surely be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear the army is coming they will breach those channels and cut off the water.

sentences.zh: 環城百里之內，地不生草，人馬飢渴，難以久留。

translations.literal: Within a hundred li around the city walls the land produces no grass; men and horses will hunger and thirst—it will be hard to remain long.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred li of the walls nothing grows; men and horses will starve and thirst and cannot stay long.

sentences.zh: 斤等之議是也。」

translations.literal: The counsel of Xi Jin and the others is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin and the others are right."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃命浩與斤等相詰難。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor thereupon ordered Hao and Xi Jin and the others to cross-examine one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Hao and Xi Jin's party to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 眾無復它言，但云「彼無水草」。

translations.literal: The assembly had no further other words but only said, "There is no water or grass there."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly had nothing more to say except, "There is no water or grass there."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「《漢書‧地理志》稱『涼州之畜為天下饒』，若無水草，畜何以蕃？

translations.literal: Hao said: "The 'Treatise on Geography' in the Book of Han states, 'The livestock of Liang Province are the richest under Heaven'—if there were no water or grass, how could livestock multiply?
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The Book of Han's Treatise on Geography says, 'The livestock of Liangzhou are the richest under Heaven'—without water and grass, how could herds multiply?

sentences.zh: 又，漢人終不於無水草之地築城郭，建郡縣也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Han people would never build walls and towers or establish commanderies and counties in a place without water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Han would never build cities and counties where there was no water or grass.

sentences.zh: 且雪之消釋，僅能斂塵，何得通渠溉灌乎！

translations.literal: And as for snow melting—it can barely gather dust; how could it open channels for irrigation!
translations.idiomatic: And melting snow can barely wet the dust—how could it feed irrigation channels!

sentences.zh: 此言大為欺誣矣。」

translations.literal: These words are a great deception and fraud."
translations.idiomatic: That is outright deception."

sentences.zh: 李順曰：「耳聞不如目見，吾嘗目見，何可共辯」浩曰：「汝受人金錢，欲為之遊說，謂我目不見便可欺邪！」

translations.literal: Li Shun said: "What the ear hears is not equal to what the eye sees—I have seen it with my own eyes; how can we debate together?" Hao said: "You received another's gold and cash and wish to plead for him—do you think that because my eyes do not see, you can deceive me!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun said, "Hearing is not like seeing—I have seen it myself; what is there to argue?" Hao said, "You took their gold and want to plead for them—do you think I am blind and can be fooled!"

sentences.zh: 帝隱聽，聞之，乃出見斤等，辭色嚴厲，群臣不敢復言，唯唯而已。。

translations.literal: The emperor listened in concealment; when he heard it, he came forth to meet Xi Jin and the others, his words and expression stern; the ministers dared not speak again and only murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been listening in secret; when he heard this he came out to face Xi Jin's party with a stern countenance, and the ministers dared say no more and only murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 群臣既出，振威將軍代人伊□言於帝曰：「涼州若果無水草，彼何以為國？

translations.literal: After the ministers had withdrawn, Zhenwei General Yi Bo of the Dai people said to the emperor: "If Liang Province truly had no water or grass, how could they maintain a state?
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers left, Zhenwei General Yi Bo, a man of the Dai, said to the emperor, "If Liangzhou truly lacked water and grass, how could they have a state?

sentences.zh: 眾議皆不可用，宜從浩言。」

translations.literal: The assembly's counsel cannot be used—Your Majesty should follow Hao's words."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly's advice should be rejected; Your Majesty should follow Hao."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丁丑，魏主治兵於西郊；

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, on dingchou, the Wei emperor reviewed troops at the western suburb;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on dingchou, the Wei emperor reviewed troops at the western suburb;

sentences.zh: 六月，甲辰，發平城。

translations.literal: sixth month, on jiachen, he set out from Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month, on jiachen, he marched from Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 使侍中宜都王穆壽輔太子晃監國，決留台事，內外聽焉。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Attendant the King of Yidu Mu Shou to assist the crown prince Huang in overseeing the state, deciding matters left at the capital, with authority within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He left Palace Attendant Prince Mu Shou of Yidu to assist Crown Prince Huang in governing, with authority over all affairs left at the capital.

sentences.zh: 又使大將軍長樂王稽敬、輔國大將軍建寧王崇將二萬人屯漠南以備柔然。

translations.literal: He also sent Grand General the King of Changle Ji Jing and Assistant State General the King of Jianning Chong to command twenty thousand men garrisoned south of the desert to guard against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He also posted Grand General Prince Ji Jing of Changle and Assistant State General Prince Chong of Jianning with twenty thousand men south of the desert to guard against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 命公卿為書以讓河西王牧犍，數其十二罪，且曰：「若親帥群臣委贄遠迎，謁拜馬首，上策也。

translations.literal: He ordered the dukes and ministers to compose a letter reproaching the King of Hexi Mujian, enumerating his twelve crimes, and saying: "If you personally lead your ministers, surrender your tokens of allegiance, and welcome us from afar, bowing at our horses' heads—that is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the high ministers to draft a reproach to Hexi king Mujian, listing twelve crimes, and saying, "If you personally lead your ministers to surrender and welcome us from afar, bowing at our horses' heads—that is the best course.

sentences.zh: 六軍既臨，面縛輿櫬，其次也。

translations.literal: When the six armies have arrived, to bind your face and come with the coffin plank—that is the next.
translations.idiomatic: When the six armies arrive, to come bound with a coffin on your back is the next best.

sentences.zh: 若守迷窮城，不時悛悟，身死族滅，為世大戮。

translations.literal: If you cling in delusion to a desperate city and do not repent in time, body dead and clan extinguished—you will be the great object of slaughter for the age.
translations.idiomatic: If you stubbornly hold a doomed city and do not repent in time, you and your clan will perish and become a warning to the world.

sentences.zh: 宜思厥中，自求多福！」。

translations.literal: You should ponder within yourself and seek your own great fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: Consider your heart and seek your own fortune!"

sentences.zh: 己酉，改封隴西王吐谷渾慕利延為河南王。。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the King of Longxi Tuyuhun Moliyan was re-enfeoffed as King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Moliyan, king of Longxi Tuyuhun, was re-enfeoffed as King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 魏主自雲中濟河，秋，七月，己巳，至上郡屬國城。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor crossed the river from Yunzhong; autumn, seventh month, on jisi, he reached Shangjun Dependency State City.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor crossed the river from Yunzhong; in autumn, the seventh month, on jisi, he reached Shangjun Dependency State City.

sentences.zh: 壬午，留輜重，部分諸軍，使撫軍大將軍永昌王健、尚書令劉絜與常山王素為前鋒，兩道並進；

translations.literal: On renwu he left the baggage train, divided the armies, and sent Pacification Army Grand General the King of Yongchang Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, and the King of Changshan Su as vanguard—two columns advancing together;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he left the baggage train, divided the forces, and sent Pacification Army Grand General Prince Wang Jian of Yongchang, Director Liu Jie, and Prince Su of Changshan as vanguard in two columns;

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍樂平王丕、太宰陽平王杜超為後繼；

translations.literal: Swift-cavalry Grand General the Prince of Leping Pi and Grand Mentor the King of Yangping Du Chao as rear guard;
translations.idiomatic: Swift-cavalry Grand General Prince Pi of Leping and Grand Mentor Prince Du Chao of Yangping as rear guard;

sentences.zh: 以平西將軍源賀為鄉導。。

translations.literal: with General Who Pacifies the West Yuan He as guide.
translations.idiomatic: with General Who Pacifies the West Yuan He as guide.

sentences.zh: 魏主問賀以取涼州方略，對曰：「姑臧城旁有四部鮮卑，皆臣祖父舊民，臣願處軍前，宣國威信，示以禍福，必相帥歸命。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor asked He for the strategy to take Liang Province. He replied: "Beside Guzang city are four divisions of Xianbei, all my grandfather's former subjects; your servant wishes to be placed before the army, proclaim the state's authority and trust, show fortune and calamity—they will surely lead one another to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked He for a plan to take Liangzhou. He replied, "Near Guzang are four Xianbei divisions, all my grandfather's former subjects; I wish to go before the army, proclaim the state's authority, and show them fortune and ruin—they will surely submit together.

sentences.zh: 外援既服，然後取其孤城，如反掌耳。」

translations.literal: Once outside support has submitted, then take their isolated city—it will be like turning the palm."
translations.idiomatic: Once their outside allies submit, taking the isolated city will be like turning one's palm."

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「善！」。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said: "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 八月，甲午，永昌王健獲河西畜產二十餘萬。。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu, Wang Jian of Yongchang obtained more than two hundred thousand head of Hexi livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu, Wang Jian of Yongchang seized more than two hundred thousand head of livestock in the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 河西王牧犍聞有魏師，驚曰：「何為乃爾！」

translations.literal: The King of Hexi Mujian heard that there were Wei troops and said in alarm: "Why has it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: King Mujian of Hexi heard that Wei forces were approaching and cried in alarm, "Why has it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 用左丞姚定國計，不肯出迎，求救於柔然。

translations.literal: He employed the plan of Left Assistant Minister Yao Dingguo, refused to go out to welcome them, and sought rescue from the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the counsel of Left Assistant Minister Yao Dingguo, refused to go out to surrender, and appealed to the Rouran for aid.

sentences.zh: 遣其弟征南大將軍董來將兵萬餘人出戰於城南，望風奔潰。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother the General Who Conquers the South Dong Lai to lead more than ten thousand troops to give battle south of the city; at sight of the enemy they fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his brother Dong Lai, General Who Conquers the South, with more than ten thousand men to fight south of the city, but they broke and fled at the first encounter.

sentences.zh: 劉絜用卜者言，以為日辰不不利，斂兵不追，董來遂得入城。

translations.literal: Liu Jie heeded the diviner's words, believing the day and hour were unfavorable, gathered the troops and did not pursue, so Dong Lai was thus able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie heeded a diviner who pronounced the day inauspicious, held his troops back, and did not pursue; Dong Lai thus made it back into the city.

sentences.zh: 魏主由是怒之。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor on this account was angry with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was furious with him for it.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏主至姑臧，遣使諭牧犍令出降。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Wei emperor arrived at Guzang and sent envoys to instruct Mujian to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the emperor reached Guzang and sent envoys ordering Mujian to surrender.

sentences.zh: 牧犍聞柔然欲入魏邊為寇，冀幸魏主東還，遂嬰城固守；

translations.literal: Mujian heard that the Rouran wished to enter the Wei frontier as raiders and hoped by good fortune that the Wei emperor would return east; he then enclosed the city and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Rouran meant to raid the Wei frontier, Mujian hoped the emperor would return east and shut himself in Guzang to hold out.

sentences.zh: 其兄子祖逾城出降，魏主具知其情，乃分軍圍之。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Zu climbed over the wall to come out and surrender; the Wei emperor fully knew his circumstances and then divided the army to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zu climbed over the wall to surrender; when the emperor learned the full situation, he divided his forces to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 源賀引兵招慰諸部下三萬餘落，故魏主得專攻姑臧，無復外慮。。

translations.literal: Yuan He led troops to summon and comfort the various subordinate peoples, more than thirty thousand clans, so the Wei emperor could concentrate on attacking Guzang alone without further outside concerns.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan He led troops to win over more than thirty thousand dependent clans, so the emperor could focus on Guzang without other distractions.

sentences.zh: 魏主見姑臧城外水草豐饒，由是恨李順，謂崔浩曰：「卿之昔言，今果驗矣。」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor saw that outside Guzang city grass and water were abundant and rich; on this account he resented Li Shun and said to Cui Hao: "Your words of former days are now truly verified."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rich grass and water outside Guzang, the emperor bore a grudge against Li Shun and told Cui Hao, "Your earlier prediction has indeed come true."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣之言不敢不實，類皆如此。」。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant's words dare not be unreal; they are mostly all like this."
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "I never speak falsely; it is mostly like this."

sentences.zh: 魏主之將伐涼州也，太子晃亦以為疑。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor was about to campaign against Liangzhou, the Crown Prince Huang also held doubts.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was planning the Liangzhou campaign, Crown Prince Huang had doubts as well.

sentences.zh: 至是，魏主賜太子詔曰：「姑臧城東、西門外，湧泉合於城北，其大如河。

translations.literal: At this time the Wei emperor bestowed an edict on the Crown Prince, saying: "East and west of Guzang city's gates, bubbling springs unite north of the city; they are as large as a river.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the emperor wrote to the crown prince: "East and west of Guzang's gates, springs surge together north of the city, as broad as a river.

sentences.zh: 自餘溝渠流入漠中，其間乃無燥地。

translations.literal: From the remaining ditches and canals water flows into the desert; in between there is then no dry ground.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller channels run off into the desert; there is scarcely dry ground between them.

sentences.zh: 故有此敕，以釋汝疑。」。
