translations.literal: Therefore there is this edict, to dispel your doubts."
translations.idiomatic: I send this to lay your doubts to rest."

sentences.zh: 庚子，立皇子鑠為南平王。。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the emperor established the imperial son Shuo as Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Prince Shuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙戌，河西王牧犍兄子萬年帥所領降魏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingxu, Mujian's nephew Wan Nian led those he commanded to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingxu, Mujian's nephew Wan Nian led his followers in surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 姑臧城潰，牧犍帥其文武五千人面縛請降，魏主釋其縛而禮之。

translations.literal: Guzang city collapsed; Mujian led his civil and military officials, five thousand men, with faces bound to request surrender; the Wei emperor released their bonds and treated them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Guzang fell; Mujian led five thousand officials and officers forward bound to beg surrender; the emperor released their bonds and received them courteously.

sentences.zh: 收其城內戶口二十餘萬，倉庫珍寶不可勝計。

translations.literal: They collected within the city more than two hundred thousand households, and storehouses of treasures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than two hundred thousand people within the walls and storehouses of treasure beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 使張掖王禿髮保周、龍騎將軍穆罷、安遠將軍源賀分徇諸郡，雜胡降者又數十萬。。

translations.literal: He sent the Prince of Zhangye Tufa Baozhou, General of Dragon Cavalry Mu Ba, and General Who Pacifies the Distance Yuan He to divide and pacify the various commanderies; miscellaneous barbarians who surrendered numbered again several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Baozhou of Zhangye, Mu Ba (General of Dragon Cavalry), and Yuan He to secure the commanderies; several hundred thousand more mixed peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 初，牧犍以其弟無諱為沙州刺史、都督建康以西諸軍事、領酒泉太守，宜得為秦州刺史、都督丹嶺以西諸軍事、領張掖太守，安周為樂都太守，從弟唐兒為敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mujian had appointed his younger brother Wuhui as Governor of Shazhou and Commander of all military affairs west of Jiankang, holding the post of Administrator of Jiuquan; Yide was to be Governor of Qinzhou and Commander of all military affairs west of Danling, holding the post of Administrator of Zhangye; Anzhou was Administrator of Ledu; his younger cousin Tang'er was Administrator of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mujian had posted his brother Wuhui as governor of Shazhou, commander west of Jiankang, and Jiuquan administrator; Yide as Qinzhou governor and Zhangye administrator; Anzhou at Ledu; and his cousin Tang'er at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 及姑臧破，魏主遣鎮南將軍代人奚眷擊張掖，鎮北將軍封沓擊樂都。

translations.literal: When Guzang fell, the Wei emperor sent the General Who Guards the South Xi Juan of the Dairen to strike Zhangye, and the General Who Guards the North Feng Ta to strike Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: When Guzang fell, the emperor sent Xi Juan south against Zhangye and Feng Ta north against Ledu.

sentences.zh: 宜得燒倉庫，西奔酒泉；

translations.literal: Yide burned the storehouses and fled west to Jiuquan;
translations.idiomatic: Yide burned the granaries and fled west to Jiuquan;

sentences.zh: 安周南奔吐谷渾，封沓掠數千戶而還。

translations.literal: Anzhou fled south to Tuyuhun; Feng Ta plundered several thousand households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhou fled south to the Tuyuhun; Feng Ta raided several thousand households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 奚眷進攻酒泉，無諱、宜得收遺民奔晉昌，遂就唐兒於敦煌。

translations.literal: Xi Juan advanced to attack Jiuquan; Wuhui and Yide gathered surviving people and fled to Jinchang, then joined Tang'er at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Juan pressed Jiuquan; Wuhui and Yide rallied survivors at Jinchang, then joined Tang'er at Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 魏主使弋陽公元絜守酒泉，及武威、張掖皆置將守之。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Yuan Jie of Yiyang to hold Jiuquan, and at Wuwei and Zhangye as well placed generals to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted Yuan Jie at Jiuquan and stationed officers at Wuwei and Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 魏主置酒姑臧，謂群臣曰：「崔公智略有餘，吾不復以為奇。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor set out wine at Guzang and said to the assembled ministers: "Minister Cui's strategems are more than adequate—I no longer find it marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in Guzang the emperor told his ministers, "Cui's strategems no longer surprise me—

sentences.zh: 伊□弓馬之士，而所見乃與崔公同，深可奇也！」

translations.literal: Yi Bo is a man of bow and horse, yet what he saw is actually the same as Minister Cui's—deeply marvelous indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi Bo is a fighting man, yet his judgment matched Cui Hao's—that is truly remarkable!"

sentences.zh: □善射，能曳牛卻行，走及奔馬，而性忠謹，故魏主特愛之。。

translations.literal: Bo excelled at shooting, could drag an ox backward while walking, run and catch up to a galloping horse, and by nature was loyal and careful—therefore the Wei emperor especially cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Bo was a fine archer who could walk backward dragging an ox and keep pace with a galloping horse; loyal and careful by nature, the emperor especially favored him.

sentences.zh: 魏主之西伐也，穆壽送至河上，魏主敕之曰：「吳提與牧犍相結素深，聞朕討牧犍，吳提必犯塞，朕故留壯兵肥馬，使卿輔佐太子。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor was campaigning west, Mu Shou escorted him to the river; the Wei emperor charged him, saying: "Wuti and Mujian have long been deeply allied; hearing that We attack Mujian, Wuti will surely violate the passes—I therefore leave strong troops and fat horses for you to assist the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign, Mu Shou escorted the emperor to the river, who instructed him: "Wuti and Mujian are old allies; when he hears I am attacking Mujian, Wuti will raid the border. I leave you strong troops and good horses to support the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 收田既畢，即發兵詣漠南，分伏要害以待虜至。

translations.literal: Once the harvest is finished, immediately deploy troops to the south of the desert and divide ambushes at strategic points to await the barbarians' arrival.
translations.idiomatic: When the harvest is in, move troops to the southern desert and set ambushes at key points for the enemy's arrival.

sentences.zh: 引使深入，然後擊之，無不克矣。

translations.literal: Draw them to advance deep, then strike—nothing will fail to be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Lure them deep, then strike, and you cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 涼州路遠，朕不得救，卿勿違朕言！」

translations.literal: Liangzhou's road is far—I cannot rescue you; do not disobey Our words!"
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou is far and I cannot save you—do not disobey me!"

sentences.zh: 壽頓首受命。

translations.literal: Shou kowtowed and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Shou kowtowed and accepted the charge.

sentences.zh: 壽雅信中書博士公孫質，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Shou by temperament trusted Palace Secretariat Academician Gongsun Zhi and made him his planning chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shou deeply trusted Academician Gongsun Zhi of the Secretariat and made him his chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 壽、質皆信卜筮，以為柔然必不來，不為之備。

translations.literal: Shou and Zhi both trusted divination and hexagrams, believing the Rouran would surely not come, and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Both trusted divination, convinced the Rouran would not come, and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 質，軌之弟也。。

translations.literal: Zhi was the younger brother of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was a younger brother of Gui.

sentences.zh: 柔然敕連可汗聞魏主向姑臧，乘虛入寇，留其兄乞列歸與嵇敬、建寧王崇相拒於北鎮，自帥精騎深入，至善無七介山，平城大駭，民爭走中城。

translations.literal: The Rouran Khan Chelian heard the Wei emperor was headed for Guzang, took the opportunity to enter as raiders, left his elder brother Qiliegui with Ji Jing and the Prince of Jianning Chong to resist at North Garrison, himself leading picked cavalry in deep penetration to Mount Qijieshan of Shanyu; Pingcheng was greatly terrified, and the people struggled to reach the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: When Khan Chelian of the Rouran heard the emperor was bound for Guzang, he invaded while the realm was exposed, leaving his brother Qiliegui with Ji Jing and Prince Chong of Jianning to hold North Garrison while he led elite cavalry deep to Mount Qijie near Shanyu; Pingcheng was thrown into panic as people rushed into the inner city.

sentences.zh: 穆壽不知所為，欲塞西郭門，請太子避保南山，竇太后不聽而止。

translations.literal: Mu Shou did not know what to do, wished to block the western outer gate, and asked the Crown Prince to avoid peril on Mount Baonan—the Empress Dowager Dou would not listen and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Shou was at a loss, proposed sealing the western gate and sending the crown prince to Mount Baonan for safety; Empress Dowager Dou refused and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 遣司空長孫道生、征北大將軍張黎拒之於吐頹山。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and Grand General Who Conquers the North Zhang Li to resist them at Mount Tufei.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Changsun Daosheng and Zhang Li to meet them at Mount Tufei.

sentences.zh: 會嵇敬、建寧王崇擊破乞列歸於陰山之北，擒之，並其伯父他吾無鹿胡及將帥五百人，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: It happened that Ji Jing and Prince Chong of Jianning routed Qiliegui north of Yinshan, captured him, and together with his paternal uncle Tawu Luhu and five hundred commanders and generals, severed heads numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jing and Prince Chong of Jianning defeated Qiliegui north of Yinshan, capturing him along with his uncle Tawu Luhu and five hundred officers, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 敕連聞之，遁去；

translations.literal: Chelian heard of it and fled away;
translations.idiomatic: Chelian heard the news and fled;

sentences.zh: 追至漠南而還。。

translations.literal: they pursued to the south of the desert and returned.
translations.idiomatic: the pursuers followed to the southern desert and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛酉，魏主東還，留樂平王丕及征西將軍賀多羅鎮涼州，徙沮渠牧犍宗族及吏民三萬戶於平城。。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on xinyou, the Wei emperor returned east, left the Prince of Leping Pi and General Who Conquers the West He Duoluo to garrison Liangzhou, and moved the clan of Juqu Mujian and civil and military people, thirty thousand households, to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinyou, the emperor returned east, leaving Prince Pi of Leping and He Duoluo to guard Liangzhou and relocating Mujian's clan and thirty thousand households of officials and people to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，禿髮保周帥諸部鮮卑據張掖叛魏。。

translations.literal: On guihai, Tufa Baozhou led the various divisions of Xianbei to occupy Zhangye and rebel against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Tufa Baozhou led Xianbei factions to seize Zhangye and rebel against Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙亥，太子劭加元服，大赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yihai, Crown Prince Shao performed the capping ceremony; a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yihai, Crown Prince Shao came of age and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 劭美鬢眉，好讀書，便弓馬，喜延賓客；

translations.literal: Shao had beautiful temples and brows, loved reading books, was skilled at bow and horse, and delighted in extending hospitality to guests;
translations.idiomatic: Shao was handsome, loved learning and horsemanship, and delighted in entertaining guests;

sentences.zh: 意之所欲，上必從之，東宮置兵與羽林等。。

translations.literal: what his mind desired, the emperor above surely followed; the Eastern Palace's deployment of troops equaled the Forest of Feathers guard.
translations.idiomatic: whatever he wished, the emperor granted; the Eastern Palace was armed on a par with the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏主至平城，以柔然入寇，無大失亡，故穆壽等得不誅。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Wei emperor arrived at Pingcheng; because the Rouran invaders caused no great losses, Mu Shou and the others were able to escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the emperor reached Pingcheng; because the Rouran raid had caused little loss, Mu Shou and his circle were spared execution.

sentences.zh: 魏主猶以妹婿待沮渠牧犍，征西大將軍、河西王如故。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor still treated Juqu Mujian as a son-in-law by marriage; General Who Conquers the West, King of Hexi—as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still treated Mujian as a son-in-law, with his titles as King of Hexi and General Who Conquers the West unchanged.

sentences.zh: 牧犍母卒，葬以太妃禮；

translations.literal: Mujian's mother died and was buried with the rites of Grand Consort;
translations.idiomatic: When Mujian's mother died, she was buried with grand consort honors;

sentences.zh: 為武宣王置守塚三十家。。

translations.literal: for the Prince of Wuxuan thirty households were established to tend the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: and thirty households were assigned to guard the tomb of the Prince of Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 涼州自張氏以來，號為多士。

translations.literal: Liangzhou since the Zhang clan's time has been styled as abundant in scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou had been known for its scholars since the days of the Zhang regime.

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍尤喜文學，以敦煌闞駰為姑臧太守，張湛為兵部尚書，劉昺、索敞、陰興為國師助教，金城宋欽為世子洗馬，趙柔為金部郎，廣平程駿、駿從弟弘為世子侍講。

translations.literal: Juqu Mujian especially delighted in literary studies; he made Kan Yin of Dunhuang Administrator of Guzang, Zhang Zhan Minister of War, Liu Bing, Suo Chang, and Yin Xing assistants to the National Teacher, Song Qin of Jincheng Crown Prince's Groom, Zhao Rou Gentleman of the Gold Bureau, and Cheng Jun of Guangping with Jun's younger cousin Hong as Crown Prince's Lecturers.
translations.idiomatic: Mujian especially loved learning; he appointed Kan Yin of Dunhuang as Guzang administrator, Zhang Zhan as minister of war, Liu Bing, Suo Chang, and Yin Xing as tutors to the national teacher, Song Qin of Jincheng as crown prince's groom, Zhao Rou as an officer of the treasury, and Cheng Jun of Guangping with his cousin Hong as lecturers to the heir.

sentences.zh: 魏主克涼州，皆禮而用之，以闞駰、劉昺為樂平王丕從事中郎。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor conquered Liangzhou, he all treated them with courtesy and employed them, appointing Kan Yin and Liu Bing as Attendants in the Prince of Leping Pi's service.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Liangzhou, the emperor honored and employed them all, making Kan Yin and Liu Bing attendants on Prince Pi of Leping.

sentences.zh: 安定胡叟，少有俊才，往從牧犍，牧犍不甚重之，叟謂程弘曰：「貴主居僻陋之國而淫名僭禮，以小事大而心不純壹，外慕仁義而實無道德，其亡可翹足待也。

translations.literal: Hu Sou of Anding, in youth possessing outstanding talent, had gone to follow Mujian; Mujian did not greatly value him. Sou said to Cheng Hong: "Your honored lord dwells in a remote and crude state yet indulges in inflated titles and usurped rites, treats a small matter as great yet his heart is not pure and single, outwardly admires benevolence and righteousness yet in reality has no virtue—his destruction can be awaited with toes raised.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sou of Anding, a gifted youth who had served Mujian without winning much favor, told Cheng Hong: "Your lord rules a remote realm yet indulges in inflated titles and usurped ceremony; he affects grandeur with an impure heart and preaches benevolence without practicing it—his fall can be awaited with toes raised.

sentences.zh: 吾將擇木，先集於魏；

translations.literal: I shall choose my tree and first gather to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: I will choose my perch and cast my lot with Wei first;

sentences.zh: 與子暫違，非久闊也。」

translations.literal: with you, my lord, I part for a time—it is not a long separation."
translations.idiomatic: a brief parting from you, my lord, not a long farewell."

sentences.zh: 遂適魏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He then went over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 歲餘而牧犍敗。

translations.literal: Within a year more Mujian was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Mujian had fallen.

sentences.zh: 魏主以叟為先識，拜虎威將軍，賜爵始復男。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor regarded Sou as foreseeing ahead, appointed him General of Tiger Might, and bestowed the title Baron of Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, crediting his foresight, made him General of Tiger Might and enfeoffed him as Baron of Shifu.

sentences.zh: 河內常爽，世寓涼州，不受禮命，魏主以為宣威將軍。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang of Henei, for generations sojourning in Liangzhou, had not accepted titles and appointments; the Wei emperor made him General Who Proclaims Might.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang of Henei, long resident in Liangzhou though he had refused office, was made General Who Proclaims Might.

sentences.zh: 河西右相宋繇從魏主至平城而卒。。

translations.literal: Song Yao, Right Chancellor of Hexi, followed the Wei emperor to Pingcheng and died.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao, former right chancellor of Hexi, followed the emperor to Pingcheng and died there.

sentences.zh: 魏主以索敞為中書博士。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor made Suo Chang a Secretariat Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Suo Chang a doctoral scholar of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時魏朝方尚武功，貴遊子弟以講學為意。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei court was just then exalting military achievement; the sons of noble houses used lecturing and study as a fashion.
translations.idiomatic: The court still prized martial glory, and young nobles took up scholarly study as a fashion.

sentences.zh: 敞為博士十餘年，勤於誘導，肅而有禮，貴游皆嚴憚之，多所成立，前後顯達至尚書、牧守者數十人。

translations.literal: Chang served as doctor for more than ten years, diligent in guidance and instruction, stern yet with propriety; the noble scions all stood in awe of him, and many were established; before and after, those who rose to prominence reaching Ministers of State and governors numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Chang taught as a doctor for more than ten years, guiding pupils with stern courtesy that awed the nobility; dozens of his students later rose to posts as ministers and regional governors.

sentences.zh: 常爽置館於溫水之右，教授七百餘人；

translations.literal: Chang Shuang established a hall on the right bank of the Wen River and instructed more than seven hundred men;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang founded a school on the Wen River's right bank with more than seven hundred pupils;

sentences.zh: 爽立賞罰之科，弟子事之如嚴君。

translations.literal: Shuang established regulations of reward and punishment; disciples served him as they would a stern lord.
translations.idiomatic: He set rules of reward and punishment, and his students treated him as a strict master.

sentences.zh: 由是魏之儒風始振。

translations.literal: From this the Confucian wind of Wei first stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Confucian learning in Wei began to revive.

sentences.zh: 高允每稱爽訓厲有方，曰：「文翁柔勝，先生剛克，立教雖殊，成人一也。」。

translations.literal: Gao Yun often praised Shuang's instruction and discipline as having method, saying: "Wen Weng overcame by gentleness; the Master overcomes by sternness—establishing teaching though different, completing men is one."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun often praised Shuang's discipline: "Wen Weng prevailed through gentleness; Master Chang through severity—different methods, but the same end in forming men."

sentences.zh: 陳留江強，寓居涼州，獻經、史、諸子千餘卷及書法，亦拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Jiang Qiang of Chenliu, residing in Liangzhou, presented the classics, histories, and masters in more than a thousand scrolls together with calligraphy models, and was also appointed Secretariat Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qiang of Chenliu, living in Liangzhou, presented more than a thousand scrolls of classics, histories, and masters' works plus model calligraphy, and was also made a Secretariat doctor.

sentences.zh: 魏主命崔浩監秘書事，綜理史職；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor ordered Cui Hao to supervise Secretariat affairs and comprehensively manage the duties of historiography;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Cui Hao in charge of the imperial library and the historiographical office;

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎高允、散騎侍郎張偉參典著作。

translations.literal: with Secretariat Gentleman Gao Yun and Cavalier Attendant Zhang Wei participating in directing composition.
translations.idiomatic: with Gao Yun and Zhang Wei assisting the historiographical project.

sentences.zh: 浩啟稱：「陰仲達、段承根，涼土美才，請同修國史。」

translations.literal: Hao submitted a memorial stating: "Yin Zhongda and Duan Chenggen are fine talents of Liang soil—request to join them in compiling the national history."
translations.idiomatic: Hao memorialized: "Yin Zhongda and Duan Chenggen are outstanding talents of Liangzhou; I ask that they help compile the dynastic history."

sentences.zh: 皆除著作郎。

translations.literal: All were appointed Composition Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Both were appointed historiographers.

sentences.zh: 仲達，武威人；

translations.literal: Zhongda was a man of Wuwei;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongda was from Wuwei;

sentences.zh: 承根，暉之子也。。

translations.literal: Chenggen was the son of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggen was the son of Duan Hui.

sentences.zh: 浩集諸歷家，考校漢元以來日月薄食、五星行度，並譏前史之失，別為《魏歷》，以示高允。

translations.literal: Hao assembled the various calendrical specialists, examined and collated from Han Yuangu onward solar and lunar eclipses and the courses of the five planets, and together criticized the errors of earlier histories, separately compiling the "Wei Calendar" to show Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Hao gathered calendrical experts, checked eclipses and planetary motions since Emperor Yuan of Han, corrected earlier chronicles' errors, and drafted a new Wei calendar for Gao Yun's review.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「漢元年十月，五星聚東井，此乃歷術之淺事；

translations.literal: Yun said: "In the first year of Han, the tenth month, the five planets gathered at the Well—this is a shallow matter of calendrical technique;
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "The five planets' gathering in the Well in the tenth month of Han's founding year is elementary calendrical lore;

sentences.zh: 今譏漢史而不覺此謬，恐後人之譏今猶今之譏古也。」

translations.literal: now you criticize Han history yet do not perceive this error—fearing that later people will criticize the present just as the present criticizes antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: yet you fault the Han histories without noticing this mistake—later ages may fault us as we fault them."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「所謬雲何？」

translations.literal: Hao said: "What error do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked, "What mistake do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「案《星傳》：『太白、辰星常附日而行。』

translations.literal: Yun said: "According to the Star Canon: 'Venus and Mercury normally travel attached to the sun.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "In the Star Canon it says, 'Venus and Mercury always keep to the sun's course.'

sentences.zh: 十月，日在尾、箕，昏沒於申南，而東井方出於寅北，二星何得背日而行？

translations.literal: In the tenth month the sun was in Wei and Ji, setting at twilight south of Shen, while the Well was just rising north of Yin—how could those two stars travel against the sun?
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the sun stood in Wei and Ji, vanished at dusk south of Shen, while the Well was only rising north of Yin—how could those two stars run counter to the sun?

sentences.zh: 是史官欲神其事，不復推之於理也。」

translations.literal: This shows the scribes wished to make the event miraculous and did not reason it through."
translations.idiomatic: The clerks wanted to make the omen supernatural and never worked it out by reason."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「天文欲為變者，何所不可邪？」

translations.literal: Hao said: "If the heavens wish to manifest a portent, what cannot happen?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "When the sky means to show a sign, what is impossible?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「此不可以空言爭，宜更審之。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "This cannot be settled by empty words; it should be examined further."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Words alone won't settle this; it needs another careful look."

sentences.zh: 坐者鹹怪允之言，唯東宮少傅游雅曰：「高君精於歷數，當不虛也。」

translations.literal: Those present all found Yun's words strange; only the Eastern Palace Junior Tutor You Ya said: "Master Gao is expert in calendrical reckoning—he is surely not speaking idly."
translations.idiomatic: The company thought Yun odd; only Junior Tutor You Ya of the Eastern Palace said, "Master Gao is a master of the calendar—he is not talking nonsense."

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，浩謂允曰：「先所論者，本不經心；

translations.literal: More than a year later, Hao said to Yun: "What we discussed before—I did not take it to heart;
translations.idiomatic: A year and more later Hao told Yun, "Our earlier talk—I never really minded it;

sentences.zh: 乃更考究，果如君言。

translations.literal: but on further study it proved exactly as you said.
translations.idiomatic: but when I looked into it again, it was exactly as you said.

sentences.zh: 五星乃以前三月聚東井，非十月也。」

translations.literal: The five planets had in fact gathered at the Well three months earlier, not in the tenth month."
translations.idiomatic: The five planets had actually met in the Well three months before—not in the tenth month."

sentences.zh: 眾乃歎服。

translations.literal: Then all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly marveled.

sentences.zh: 允雖明歷，初不推步及為人論說，唯游雅知之。

translations.literal: Though Yun understood the calendar, he had at first not engaged in computation or lectured others—only You Ya knew.
translations.idiomatic: Yun understood the calendar, yet he had never done calculations or lectured for others—only You Ya knew it.

sentences.zh: 雅數以災異問允，允曰：「陰陽災異，知之甚難；

translations.literal: You Ya often asked Yun about portents; Yun said: "Yin-yang disasters and prodigies are very hard to know;
translations.idiomatic: You Ya often asked Yun about omens; Yun said, "Yin-yang portents are very hard to know;

sentences.zh: 既已知之，復恐漏洩，不如不知也。

translations.literal: once known, one fears leakage—better not to know.
translations.idiomatic: once you know them, you fear letting the secret out—better not to know.

sentences.zh: 天下妙理至多，何遽問此！」

translations.literal: There are endless subtle principles under heaven—why rush to ask this!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth hold endless subtleties—why press this one point!"

sentences.zh: 雅乃止。

translations.literal: You Ya then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya left off.

sentences.zh: 魏主問允：「為政何先？」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor asked Yun: "In governing, what comes first?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor asked Yun, "What should come first in government?"

sentences.zh: 時魏多封禁良田，允曰：「臣少賤，唯知農事。

translations.literal: At the time Wei had many seals on good farmland; Yun said: "Your servant was humble in youth and knows only farming.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had sealed off much good land; Yun said, "I was lowborn in youth and know only agriculture.

sentences.zh: 若國家廣田積穀，公私有備，則饑饉不足憂矣。」

translations.literal: If the state broadly cultivates fields and stores grain so public and private alike are provisioned, famine need not be feared."
translations.idiomatic: If the state opens fields and hoards grain so court and people alike are stocked, hunger need not trouble us."

sentences.zh: 帝乃命悉除田禁以賦百姓。。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered all field restrictions lifted to allocate land to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered every field restriction removed and land assigned to the people.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕利延聞魏克涼州，大懼，帥眾西遁，逾沙漠。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun king Murong Lilian heard Wei had taken Liangzhou, was greatly afraid, led his people west in flight across the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lilian, king of Tuyuhun, heard that Wei had taken Liangzhou; in great fear he led his host west across the desert.

sentences.zh: 魏主以其兄慕瑰有擒赫連定之功，遣使撫諭之，慕利延乃還故地。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, because his brother Murong Gui had the merit of capturing Helian Ding, sent envoys to comfort and instruct him; Lilian then returned to his former lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor, noting that Lilian's brother Murong Gui had captured Helian Ding, sent envoys to reassure him, and Lilian returned to his old territory.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊難當將兵數萬寇魏上邽，秦州人多應之。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Nan'dang led tens of thousands to raid Wei's Shanggui; many in Qinzhou responded.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Yang Nan'dang marched tens of thousands against Wei's Shanggui, and much of Qinzhou rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 東平呂羅漢說鎮將拓跋意頭曰：「難當眾甚，今不出戰，示之以弱，眾情離沮，不可守也。」

translations.literal: Dongping Lü Luohan urged the garrison commander Tuoba Yitou: "Nan'dang's host is very large; if we do not fight now and show weakness, the people's hearts will scatter in dismay and the place cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Luohan of Dongping urged the garrison commander Tuoba Yitou, "Nan'dang's force is huge; if we refuse battle now and look weak, morale will collapse and we cannot hold the city."

sentences.zh: 意頭遣羅漢將精騎千餘出沖難當陳，所向披靡，殺其左右騎八人，難當大驚。

translations.literal: Yitou sent Luohan with a thousand-odd elite cavalry to charge Nan'dang's formation; wherever they struck the enemy broke, killing eight of his close riders—Nan'dang was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yitou sent Luohan with a thousand picked horsemen to smash Nan'dang's line; they swept all before them and killed eight of his bodyguards—Nan'dang was shaken.

sentences.zh: 會魏主以璽書責讓難當，難當引還仇池。。

translations.literal: Just then the Wei emperor sent an imperial-seal letter reproaching Nan'dang; he withdrew to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Wei emperor sent a sealed imperial letter rebuking Nan'dang, and he withdrew to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 南豐太妃司馬氏卒，故營陽王之後也。。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort of Nanfeng, née Sima, died—she had been consort to the former Prince of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Consort Sima of Nanfeng died; she had been wife to the former Prince of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 趙廣、張尋等復謀反，伏誅。。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang, Zhang Xun, and others again plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang, Zhang Xun, and others plotted rebellion again and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之上元嘉十七年（庚辰，公元四四零年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 17 (gengchen; AD 440).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia 17 (gengchen; AD 440).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己酉，沮渠無諱寇魏酒泉，元絜輕之，出城與語；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiyou, Juqu Wuji raided Wei's Jiuquan; Yuan Jie slighted him and went out of the city to speak with him;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiyou, Juqu Wuji attacked Jiuquan; Yuan Jie despised him and went outside the walls to parley;

sentences.zh: 壬子，無諱執絜以圍酒泉。。

translations.literal: on renzi, Wuji seized Jie and besieged Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: on renzi Wuji seized Jie and besieged Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏假通直常侍邢穎來聘。。

translations.literal: Second month, Wei's acting Tongzhi Changshi Xing Ying came on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Xing Ying of Wei, acting palace attendant, came on an embassy.

sentences.zh: 三月，沮渠無諱拔酒泉。。

translations.literal: Third month, Juqu Wuji took Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Juqu Wuji captured Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day wuwu—a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day wuwu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，沮渠無諱寇魏張掖，禿髮保周屯刪丹；

translations.literal: On gengchen, Wuji raided Zhangye; Tufa Baozhou encamped at Shandan;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Wuji attacked Zhangye; Tufa Baozhou held Shandan;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏主遣撫軍大將軍永昌王健督諸將討之。。

translations.literal: on bingxu, the Wei emperor sent Pacification Army Grand General Wang Jian of Yongchang to direct the generals against him.
translations.idiomatic: on bingxu the Wei emperor sent Grand General Wang Jian of Yongchang to command the campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 司徒義康專總朝權。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Liu Yikang monopolized court power.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yikang held the court in his grasp.

sentences.zh: 上羸疾積年，心勞輒發，屢至危殆；

translations.literal: The emperor had been frail for years; whenever worry taxed him it flared up, repeatedly bringing him near death;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been failing for years; worry would trigger relapses and often bring him to death's door;

sentences.zh: 義康盡心營奉，藥食非口所親嘗不進，或連夕不寐，內外眾事皆專決施行。

translations.literal: Yikang devoted himself to nursing him—medicine and food he did not taste with his own mouth were not offered; sometimes he went nights without sleep; all inner and outer affairs he decided and executed alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang nursed him devotedly—food and medicine passed his own lips before they reached the emperor; he sometimes went whole nights without sleep; he decided and carried out every matter, within the palace and without.

sentences.zh: 性好吏職，糾剔文案，莫不精盡。

translations.literal: He loved clerical work; scrutinizing documents, nothing was not done with utmost precision.
translations.idiomatic: He loved administrative work and went through every document with relentless care.

sentences.zh: 上由是多委以事，凡所陳奏，入無不可；

translations.literal: The emperor therefore entrusted him with much; whatever he memorialized was accepted without fail;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore gave him more and more; nothing he submitted was refused;

sentences.zh: 方伯以下，並令義康選用，生殺大事，或以錄命斷之。

translations.literal: governors and below all were appointed by Yikang; matters of life and death he sometimes decided by recorded order.
translations.idiomatic: provincial governors and below were chosen by Yikang; even questions of life and death he sometimes settled by written order.

sentences.zh: 勢傾遠近，朝野輻湊，每旦府門常有車數百乘，義康傾身引接，未嘗懈倦。

translations.literal: His power tilted near and far; court and countryside converged on him; each dawn hundreds of carriages stood at his mansion gate; Yikang bent himself to receive guests, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: His power overshadowed the realm; court and country flocked to him; every morning hundreds of carriages crowded his gate, and Yikang received them all himself, never tiring.

sentences.zh: 復能強記，耳目所經，終身不忘；

translations.literal: He could also remember strongly—what eye and ear passed over he never forgot for life;
translations.idiomatic: He had a prodigious memory—whatever reached his eyes or ears he never forgot;

sentences.zh: 好於稠人廣席，標題所憶以示聰明。

translations.literal: he loved in dense crowds and broad assemblies to headline what he recalled to display his brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: and in crowded halls he loved to recite what he remembered to show how clever he was.

sentences.zh: 士之幹練者，多被意遇。

translations.literal: Capable gentlemen were often favored by his special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Capable men often won his special favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂劉湛曰：「王敬弘、王球之屬，竟何所堪！

translations.literal: He once said to Liu Zhan: "Men like Wang Jinghong and Wang Qiu—what are they good for!
translations.idiomatic: He once told Liu Zhan, "What use are men like Wang Jinghong and Wang Qiu!

sentences.zh: 坐取富貴，復那可解！」

translations.literal: Sitting to reap wealth and rank—how else could it be explained!"
translations.idiomatic: They sit back and rake in rank and riches—who can explain that!"

sentences.zh: 然素無學術，不識大體，朝士有才用者皆引入己府，府僚無施及忤旨者乃斥為台官。

translations.literal: Yet he had no learning by nature and did not grasp the larger design; talented court officials were all drawn into his mansion; mansion staff with nothing to offer or who offended his intent were only expelled to terrace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had little learning and no sense of the larger frame; he pulled every able courtier into his own house, while staff who had nothing to give or who crossed him were shunted off to terrace posts.

sentences.zh: 自謂兄弟至親，不復存君臣形跡，率心而行，曾無猜防。

translations.literal: He deemed himself and his brother utterly close and no longer kept the forms of ruler and minister—acting as his heart led, never wary.
translations.idiomatic: He thought brotherly closeness meant he need not keep ruler-and-minister forms; he followed his impulses and never guarded himself.

sentences.zh: 私置僮六千餘人，不以言台，四方獻饋，皆以上品薦義康，而以次者供御；

translations.literal: He privately kept more than six thousand bondservants without reporting to the terrace; tribute from all quarters he sent the finest to Yikang and the second rank to the imperial household;
translations.idiomatic: He kept more than six thousand private retainers without informing the court; gifts from every quarter went first in quality to Yikang, and only second best to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 上嘗冬月啖甘，歎其形味並劣，義康曰：「今年甘殊有佳者。」

translations.literal: The emperor once ate sweet oranges in winter and sighed that shape and flavor were alike poor; Yikang said: "This year there are especially fine oranges."
translations.idiomatic: Once in winter the emperor ate oranges and sighed that they looked and tasted poor; Yikang said, "This year there are especially fine ones."

sentences.zh: 遣人還東府取甘，大供御者三寸。。

translations.literal: He sent someone back to the Eastern Mansion to fetch oranges—the largest for the emperor were three inches.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a man to the Eastern Mansion for oranges; the finest for the emperor measured three inches across.

sentences.zh: 領軍劉湛與僕射殷景仁有隙，湛欲倚義康之重以傾之。

translations.literal: General-in-chief Liu Zhan and Secretariat Director Yin Jingren were at odds; Zhan wished to lean on Yikang's weight to topple him.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Liu Zhan and Secretariat Director Yin Jingren were estranged; Zhan hoped to use Yikang's power to bring Yin down.

sentences.zh: 義康權勢已盛，湛愈推崇之，無復人臣之禮，上浸不能平。

translations.literal: As Yikang's power grew ever greater, Zhan extolled him more, no longer keeping minister's propriety—the emperor inwardly could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: As Yikang's power swelled, Zhan flattered him ever more openly, forgetting a subject's decorum, and the emperor grew quietly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 湛初入朝，上恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: When Zhan first entered court, imperial grace and courtesy were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan first came to court the emperor favored him generously.

sentences.zh: 湛善論治道，諳前代故事，敘致銓理，聽者忘疲。

translations.literal: Zhan was skilled at discussing governance, versed in earlier dynasties' precedents; his narration was ordered and clear—listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was eloquent on statecraft and steeped in earlier dynasties' precedents; his talk was so clear and orderly that listeners forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 每入雲龍門，御者即解駕，左右及羽儀隨意分散，不夕不出，以此為常。

translations.literal: Each entry at Yunlong Gate, the driver would unharness; attendants and guard of honor scattered at will; he did not leave before evening—this was his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered Yunlong Gate the driver would unhitch; attendants and guards wandered off at will; he never left before nightfall—it was his habit.

sentences.zh: 及晚節驅煽義康，上意雖內離而接遇不改，嘗謂所親曰：「劉班方自西還，吾與語，常視日早晚，慮其將去；

translations.literal: In his later years, inciting Yikang, though the emperor inwardly drew apart his reception did not change; he once told intimates: "Liu Ban had just returned from the west; when I talked with him I always watched whether the sun was early or late, fearing he would leave;
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, as he stirred up Yikang, the emperor inwardly turned away yet treated him as before; he once told intimates, "When Liu Ban had just returned from the west, I would watch the sun, afraid he would leave;

sentences.zh: 比入，吾亦視日早晚，苦其不去。」。

translations.literal: now when he enters I also watch the sun—vexed that he will not go."
translations.idiomatic: now when he comes in I watch the sun too, vexed that he won't go."

sentences.zh: 殷景仁密言於上曰：「相王權重，非社稷計，宜少加裁抑。」

translations.literal: Yin Jingren said secretly to the emperor: "The Prince's power is heavy—not planning for the altars; he should be restrained somewhat."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren said privately to the emperor, "The Prince's weight threatens the realm; he should be checked a little."

sentences.zh: 上陰然之。。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor silently assented.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史劉斌，湛之宗也；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal's Left Chief Clerk Liu Bin was of Zhan's clan;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin, the Grand Marshal's left chief clerk, was kin to Zhan;

sentences.zh: 大將軍從事中郎王履，謐之孫也；

translations.literal: Grand General's Attendant Gentleman Wang Lü was the grandson of Wang Mi;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lü, attendant gentleman to the Grand General, was Wang Mi's grandson;

sentences.zh: 及主簿劉敬文，祭酒魯郡孔胤秀，皆以傾諂有寵於義康；

translations.literal: and Chief Clerk Liu Jingwen, Libationer Kong Yinxiu of Lu—all through fawning had favor with Yikang;
translations.idiomatic: and Chief Clerk Liu Jingwen and Libationer Kong Yinxiu of Lu—all won Yikang's favor through flattery;

sentences.zh: 見上多疾，皆謂「宮車一日晏駕，宜立長君。」

translations.literal: seeing the emperor often ill, all said: "When the palace carriage one day pauses at evening, a mature heir should be established."
translations.idiomatic: seeing how often the emperor fell ill, they all said, "When the imperial carriage halts one evening, an elder prince ought to be enthroned."

sentences.zh: 上嘗疾篤，使義康具顧命詔。

translations.literal: The emperor was once critically ill and had Yikang draft the testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor was gravely ill he had Yikang prepare the deathbed edict.

sentences.zh: 義康還省，流涕以告湛及景仁。

translations.literal: Yikang returned to his quarters and, weeping, told Zhan and Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang went back to his offices and, in tears, told Zhan and Jingren.

sentences.zh: 湛曰：「天下艱難，詎是幼主所御！」

translations.literal: Zhan said: "The realm is hard—how can a young lord rule it!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "The realm is in peril—how could a child hold it!"

sentences.zh: 義康、景仁並不答。

translations.literal: Yikang and Jingren both did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang and Jingren said nothing.

sentences.zh: 而胤秀等輒就尚書義曹索晉鹹康末立康帝舊事，義康不知也；

translations.literal: Yet Yinxiu and the rest at once went to the Secretariat Duty Office to seek the Jin Xian'kang-era precedent for enthroning Emperor Kang—Yikang knew nothing of it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yinxiu and his circle at once went to the Secretariat archives for the Jin precedent of enthroning Emperor Kang at the end of Xian'kang—Yikang knew nothing of it;

sentences.zh: 及上疾瘳，微聞之。

translations.literal: when the emperor recovered he caught faint word of it.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor recovered he caught a whisper of it.

sentences.zh: 而斌等密謀，欲使大業終歸義康，遂邀結朋黨，伺察禁省，有不與己同者，必百方構陷之，又採拾景仁短長，或虛造異同以告湛。

translations.literal: Bin and the rest secretly plotted to make the great enterprise ultimately return to Yikang; they then formed factions, spied on the forbidden precincts—whoever did not agree with them was framed by a hundred stratagems; they also gathered Jingren's faults and strengths, sometimes fabricating differences to report to Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and the rest secretly schemed to steer the succession to Yikang; they formed factions, watched the inner palace, and framed in every way anyone who disagreed; they collected Yin's faults and merits, sometimes inventing charges to report to Zhan.

sentences.zh: 自是主、相之勢分矣。。

translations.literal: From this the sovereign's and the minister's forces divided.
translations.idiomatic: From then on sovereign and minister drew apart.

sentences.zh: 義康欲以劉斌為丹陽尹，言次，啟上陳其家貧。

translations.literal: Yikang wished to make Liu Bin Governor of Danyang; in passing he memorialized that his family was poor.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang wanted Liu Bin as governor of Danyang and, in passing, told the emperor the man was poor.

sentences.zh: 言未卒，上曰：「以為吳郡。」

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking the emperor said: "Make him Governor of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the emperor said, "Make him governor of Wu."

sentences.zh: 後會稽太守羊玄保求還，義康又欲以斌代之，啟上曰：「養玄保欲還，不審以誰為會稽？」

translations.literal: Later when Kuaiji Governor Yang Xuanbao asked to return, Yikang again wished Bin to replace him and memorialized: "Yang Xuanbao wishes to return—who should be Kuaiji?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Kuaiji governor Yang Xuanbao asked to go home, Yikang again wanted Bin in his place and asked the emperor, "Yang Xuanbao wants to leave—who should take Kuaiji?"

sentences.zh: 上時未有所擬，倉猝曰：「我已用王鴻。」

translations.literal: The emperor had no candidate ready and blurted: "I have already appointed Wang Hong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no one in mind and blurted, "I have already appointed Wang Hong."

sentences.zh: 自去年秋，上不復往東府。。

translations.literal: From last autumn the emperor no longer went to the Eastern Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: From the previous autumn the emperor never again visited the Eastern Mansion.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸巳，劉湛遭母憂去職。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on guisi, Liu Zhan left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guisi, Liu Zhan left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 湛自知罪釁已彰，無復全地，謂所親曰：「今年必敗。

translations.literal: Zhan knew his guilt was already manifest and there was no safe ground left; he told intimates: "This year I am surely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan knew his guilt was plain and he had no refuge left; he told intimates, "This year I am finished.

sentences.zh: 常日正賴口舌爭之，故得推遷耳；

translations.literal: Ordinarily I relied on verbal dispute to get promoted;
translations.idiomatic: Ordinarily I lived by arguing my way forward, and so I rose;

sentences.zh: 今既窮毒，無復此望，禍至其能久乎！」

translations.literal: now cornered, that hope is gone—when disaster comes can it wait long!"
translations.idiomatic: now I am cornered and that hope is gone—when ruin comes, can it wait long!"

sentences.zh: 乙巳，沮渠無諱復圍張掖，不克，退保臨松。

translations.literal: On yisi, Juqu Wuji again besieged Zhangye, failed, and withdrew to guard Linsong.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Juqu Wuji besieged Zhangye again, failed, and fell back to Linsong.

sentences.zh: 魏主不復加討，但以詔諭之。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor did not pursue further but only sent an edict instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent no further campaign, only an edict of warning.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁丑，魏皇孫浚生，大赦，改元太平真君，取寇謙之《神書》云「輔佐北方太平真君」故也。。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on dingchou, the Northern Wei imperial grandson Jun was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed; the era name was changed to Taiping Zhenjun, taking this from Kou Qianzhi's Divine Book, which says "assist the Northern Peaceful True Lord."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingchou, the Northern Wei imperial grandson Jun was born. A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Taiping Zhenjun, after Kou Qianzhi's Divine Book, which speaks of "assisting the Northern Peaceful True Lord."

sentences.zh: 太子劭詣京口拜京陵，司徒義康、竟陵王誕等並從，南兗州刺史、江夏王義恭自江都會之。。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Shao went to Jingkou to pay respects at the Jing tomb; the Minister of Works Yikang, the Prince of Jingling Dan, and others all followed; the Inspector of Southern Yan Province, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, joined them from Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shao went to Jingkou to pay his respects at the Jing tomb. Minister of Works Liu Yikang, Prince of Jingling Liu Dan, and others accompanied him, while Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and inspector of Southern Yan Province, met them from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，魏永昌王健擊破禿髮保周於番禾；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on jichou, the Northern Wei Prince of Yongchang Jian defeated Tufa Baozhou at Fanhe;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, the Northern Wei Prince of Yongchang, Tuoba Jian, defeated Tufa Baozhou at Fanhe;

sentences.zh: 保周走，遣安南將軍尉眷追之。。

translations.literal: Baozhou fled; he sent the General Who Pacifies the South Yu Juan in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou fled, and Jian sent the General Who Pacifies the South, Yu Juan, in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏太后竇氏殂。。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Wei Empress Dowager, Lady Dou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the Northern Wei empress dowager, Lady Dou, died.

sentences.zh: 壬子，皇后袁氏殂。。

translations.literal: On renzi, the empress née Yuan died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the empress née Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，禿髮保周窮迫自殺。。

translations.literal: On guichou, Tufa Baozhou, driven to extremity, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Tufa Baozhou, cornered and desperate, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲申，沮渠無諱使其中尉梁偉詣魏永昌王健請降，歸酒泉郡及所虜將士元絜等。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiashen, Juqu Wuhui sent his palace chamberlain Liang Wei to the Northern Wei Prince of Yongchang Jian to surrender, returning Jiuquan commandery and the captured officer Yuan Jie and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiashen, Juqu Wuhui sent his palace chamberlain Liang Wei to the Northern Wei Prince of Yongchang, Tuoba Jian, to submit. He returned Jiuquan commandery along with the captured officer Yuan Jie and others.

sentences.zh: 魏主使尉眷留鎮涼州。。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor had Yu Juan remain to garrison Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor ordered Yu Juan to remain and garrison Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬子，葬元皇后。。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on renzi, the Yuan empress was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renzi, the Yuan empress was buried.

sentences.zh: 上以司徒彭城王義康嫌隙已著，將成禍亂。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that the rift with the Minister of Works, the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, was already evident and would become calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that the breach with Liu Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng and minister of works, was already plain and would soon become catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊申，收劉湛付廷尉，下詔暴其罪惡，就獄誅之，並誅其子黯、亮、儼及其黨劉斌、劉敬文、孔胤秀等八人；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on wushen, Liu Zhan was seized and handed to the Court of Judicial Review; an edict exposed his crimes; he was executed in prison, along with his sons An, Liang, and Yan and his partisans Liu Bin, Liu Jingwen, Kong Yinxiu, and eight others in all;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, Liu Zhan was arrested and handed to the Court of Judicial Review. An edict laid bare his crimes, and he was executed in prison. His sons Liu An, Liu Liang, and Liu Yan were put to death as well, together with his partisans Liu Bin, Liu Jingwen, Kong Yinxiu, and eight others in all;

sentences.zh: 徙尚書庫部郎何默子等五人於廣州，因大赦。

translations.literal: He Mozi, lang of the Department of Storehouses under the Masters of Writing, and four others were exiled to Guangzhou; thereupon a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He Mozi, lang of the Department of Storehouses, and four others were exiled to Guangzhou, followed by a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 是日，敕義康入宿，留止中書省。

translations.literal: That day an edict ordered Yikang to lodge overnight and remain at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor ordered Yikang to stay overnight and remain at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其夕，分收湛等；

translations.literal: That evening Liu Zhan and the rest were seized in succession;
translations.idiomatic: That evening Liu Zhan and his associates were seized one after another;

sentences.zh: 青州刺史杜驥勒兵殿內以備非常，遣人宣旨告義康以湛等罪狀。

translations.literal: the Inspector of Qing Province Du Ji led troops within the palace to guard against the unexpected and sent men to announce the imperial command to Yikang, reporting Zhan's and the others' crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, inspector of Qing Province, mustered troops inside the palace to guard against any surprise and sent men to announce the imperial command to Yikang, setting forth the crimes of Zhan and his circle.

sentences.zh: 義康上表遜位，詔以義康為江州刺史，侍中、大將軍如故，出鎮豫章。。

translations.literal: Yikang submitted a memorial yielding his position; an edict appointed Yikang Inspector of Jiang Province, with Palace Attendant and Grand General as before, to go out and guard Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang submitted a memorial resigning his post. An edict made him inspector of Jiang Province while retaining his titles of palace attendant and grand general, and sent him out to take up residence at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 初，殷景仁臥疾五年，雖不見上，而密函去來，日以十數，朝政大小，必以咨之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yin Jingren had lain ill five years; though he did not appear before the emperor, secret letters went back and forth by the tens each day; great and small matters of court governance were invariably referred to him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yin Jingren had been bedridden for five years. Though he did not appear before the emperor, secret letters passed back and forth by the dozen each day, and every matter of state, great or small, was referred to him;

sentences.zh: 影跡周密，莫有窺其際者。

translations.literal: the tracks were close and tight—no one could spy into his affairs.
translations.idiomatic: his movements were so tightly concealed that no one could glimpse what he was doing.

sentences.zh: 收湛之日，景仁使拂拭衣冠，左右皆不曉其意。

translations.literal: On the day Zhan was seized, Jingren had his clothes brushed and hat adjusted; those around him did not understand his intent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Liu Zhan was arrested, Jingren had his robes brushed and his cap straightened, and those around him could not fathom his meaning.

sentences.zh: 其夜，上出華林園延賢堂，召景仁。

translations.literal: That night the emperor went out to the Garden of Flourishing Talents, Hall of Worthies Extended, and summoned Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor went to the Hall of Worthies Extended in the Garden of Flourishing Talents and summoned Jingren.

sentences.zh: 景仁猶稱腳疾，以小床輿就坐；

translations.literal: Jingren still claimed foot ailment and was brought in seated on a small litter-bed;
translations.idiomatic: Jingren still pleaded foot ailment and was carried in on a small litter to take his seat;

sentences.zh: 誅討處分，一皆委之。。

translations.literal: executions and dispositions were wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: the executions and dispositions were wholly entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 初，檀道濟薦吳興沈慶之忠謹曉兵，上使領隊防東掖門。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tan Daoji had recommended Shen Qingzhi of Wuxing as loyal, discreet, and skilled in war; the emperor had him lead the guard at the eastern side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tan Daoji had recommended Shen Qingzhi of Wuxing as loyal, prudent, and versed in warfare, and the emperor had him lead the guard at the eastern side gate.

sentences.zh: 劉湛為領軍，嘗謂之曰：「卿在省歲久，比當相論。」

translations.literal: Liu Zhan as Commander of the Palace Guards once said to him: "You have been in the Secretariat many years—it is about time you should be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: As commander of the palace guards, Liu Zhan once told him, "You have been at the Secretariat a long time—it is about time something was done for you."

sentences.zh: 慶之正色曰：「下官在省十年，自應得轉，不復以此仰累！」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said sternly: "This subordinate has been in the Secretariat ten years—I ought to be promoted on my own; I will not again burden you for this!"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said sternly, "This subordinate has served at the Secretariat ten years and ought to advance on his own merits. I will not lean on you for that again!"

sentences.zh: 收湛之夕，上開門召慶之，慶之戎服縛褲而入，上曰：「卿何意乃爾急裝？」

translations.literal: On the evening Zhan was seized, the emperor opened the gate and summoned Qingzhi; Qingzhi entered in military dress with trousers tied; the emperor said: "What do you mean by dressing so hastily?"
translations.idiomatic: On the night Liu Zhan was arrested, the emperor opened the gate and summoned Qingzhi. Qingzhi entered in military dress with his trousers tied, and the emperor said, "Why are you dressed in such haste?"

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「夜半喚隊主，不容緩服。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Summoning the unit commander at midnight—one cannot dress at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied, "When the unit commander is summoned at midnight, one cannot dress at leisure."

sentences.zh: 上遣慶之收劉斌，殺之。。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Qingzhi to seize Liu Bin and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Qingzhi to seize Liu Bin and execute him.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍徐湛之，逵之之子也，與義康尤親厚，上深銜之。

translations.literal: The Valiant Cavalry General Xu Zhizhi, son of Xu Daozhi, was especially intimate with Yikang; the emperor bore deep resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhizhi, valiant cavalry general and son of Xu Daozhi, was especially close to Yikang, and the emperor deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 義康敗，湛之被收，罪當死。

translations.literal: When Yikang fell, Zhizhi was seized; the crime called for death.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang fell, Zhizhi was arrested, and the crime called for death.

sentences.zh: 其母會稽公主，于兄弟為長嫡，素為上所禮，家事大小，必咨而後行。

translations.literal: His mother the Princess of Kuaiji was the eldest legitimate daughter among her brothers and was always treated with ritual by the emperor; domestic affairs great and small had to be consulted with her before action.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, the Princess of Kuaiji, was the eldest legitimate daughter among the imperial siblings and had always been treated with ceremony by the emperor; no household matter, great or small, was undertaken without consulting her first.

sentences.zh: 高祖征時，嘗自於新洲伐荻，有納布衫襖，臧皇后手所作也；

translations.literal: When the founder was on campaign, he once cut reeds at Xinzhou himself; there was a padded coat of raw-cloth shirt, made by the hand of Empress Zang;
translations.idiomatic: When the founder was on campaign, he once cut reeds at Xinzhou with his own hands. There was a padded coat of homespun cloth that Empress Zang had made herself;

sentences.zh: 既貴，以付公主曰：「後世有驕奢不節，可以此衣示之。」

translations.literal: after he became eminent he gave it to the princess, saying: "If later generations are proud and extravagant beyond measure, this garment may be shown them."
translations.idiomatic: after he rose to eminence he gave it to the princess, saying, "If later generations grow proud and extravagant beyond measure, show them this garment."

sentences.zh: 至是，公主入宮見上，號哭，不復施臣妾之禮，以錦囊盛納衣擲地曰：「汝家本貧賤，此是我母為汝父所作；

translations.literal: At this the princess entered the palace to see the emperor, wailing; she no longer performed the ritual of subject and concubine; she took the padded coat in a brocade pouch and flung it to the ground, saying: "Your house was originally poor and base—this is what my mother made for your father;
translations.idiomatic: Now the princess entered the palace to see the emperor, wailing. She no longer performed the ritual of subject and consort. She took the padded coat in a brocade pouch, flung it to the ground, and said, "Your house was poor and base to begin with—this is what my mother made for your father;

sentences.zh: 今日得一飽餐，遽欲殺我兒邪！」

translations.literal: today having eaten your fill at last, you would suddenly kill my son!"
translations.idiomatic: now that you have eaten your fill at last, you would suddenly kill my son!"

sentences.zh: 上乃赦之。。

translations.literal: The emperor then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王球，履之叔父也，以簡淡有美名，為上所重。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Civil Office Wang Qiu was uncle to Wang Lü; for simplicity and restraint he had a fine reputation and was deeply valued by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu, minister of the civil office and uncle to Wang Lü, was known for his simplicity and restraint and was deeply valued by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 履性進利，深結義康及湛；

translations.literal: Lü by nature advanced and profited; he deeply attached himself to Yikang and Zhizhi;
translations.idiomatic: Lü was ambitious by nature and had bound himself closely to Yikang and Zhizhi;

sentences.zh: 球屢戒之，不從。

translations.literal: Qiu repeatedly admonished him, but he would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu warned him again and again, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 誅湛之夕，履徒跣告球，球命左右為取履，先溫酒與之，謂曰：「常日語汝雲何？」

translations.literal: On the evening Zhizhi was executed, Lü came barefoot to tell Qiu; Qiu ordered attendants to fetch shoes for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said: "What did I tell you every day?"
translations.idiomatic: On the night Xu Zhizhi was executed, Lü came barefoot to Qiu. Qiu ordered attendants to fetch shoes for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said, "What did I tell you day after day?"

sentences.zh: 履怖跣告球，球命左右為取履，先溫酒與之，謂曰：「常日語汝雲何？」

translations.literal: Lü, terrified, came barefoot to tell Qiu; Qiu ordered attendants to fetch shoes for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said: "What did I tell you every day?"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Lü came barefoot to Qiu. Qiu ordered attendants to fetch shoes for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said, "What did I tell you day after day?"

sentences.zh: 履怖懼不得答。

translations.literal: Lü was terrified and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Lü was too frightened to answer.

sentences.zh: 球徐曰：「阿父在，汝亦何憂！」

translations.literal: Qiu said calmly: "While your uncle-father is here, what do you have to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu said calmly, "While your uncle is here, what do you have to fear!"

sentences.zh: 上以球故，履得免死，廢於家。。

translations.literal: Because of Qiu, the emperor spared Lü's life and had him cashiered at home.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Qiu, the emperor spared Lü's life and had him dismissed to live at home.

sentences.zh: 義康方用事，人爭求親暱，唯司徒主簿江湛早能自疏，求出為武陵內史。

translations.literal: While Yikang was in power, people vied to seek his closeness; only the Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Jiang Pu had early distanced himself and asked to go out as grand administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: While Yikang held power, everyone vied for his favor. Only Jiang Pu, chief clerk to the minister of works, had early kept his distance and asked to leave for a post as grand administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟嘗為其子求婚於湛，湛固辭，道濟因義康以請之，湛拒之愈堅，故不染於二公之難。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji once sought marriage for his son with Pu; Pu firmly declined; Daoji thereupon asked through Yikang, but Pu refused all the more firmly—thus he was not stained by the disaster of the two lords.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji once sought a marriage alliance with Pu for his son, but Pu firmly declined. Daoji then pressed the matter through Yikang, yet Pu refused all the more firmly and so was not caught in the ruin of the two great lords.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he commended him.

sentences.zh: 湛，夷之子也。。

translations.literal: Pu was son of Jiang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was the son of Jiang Yi.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康停省十餘日，見上奉辭，便下渚；

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang stopped at the Secretariat more than ten days; when he saw the emperor to bid farewell, he went down to the ford;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, remained at the Secretariat more than ten days. When he came to bid the emperor farewell, he went down to the landing;

sentences.zh: 上唯對之慟哭，餘無所言。

translations.literal: the emperor only faced him and wept bitterly; beyond that he said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor only faced him and wept bitterly, saying nothing more.

sentences.zh: 上遣沙門慧琳視之，義康曰：「弟子有還理不？」

translations.literal: The emperor sent the monk Huilin to visit him; Yikang said: "Does your disciple have any prospect of return?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the monk Huilin to visit him. Yikang said, "Does your disciple have any prospect of return?"

sentences.zh: 慧琳曰：「恨公不讀數百卷書！」。

translations.literal: Huilin said: "A pity that you did not read several hundred scrolls of books!"
translations.idiomatic: Huilin replied, "A pity you did not read a few hundred scrolls of books!"

sentences.zh: 初，吳興太守謝述，裕之弟也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Governor of Wuxing Xie Shu was younger brother to Xie Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xie Shu, governor of Wuxing, was the younger brother of Xie Yu.

sentences.zh: 累佐義康，數有規益，早卒。

translations.literal: He repeatedly assisted Yikang with admonitions that brought profit, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: He had long served Yikang with repeated counsel that brought benefit, and died young.

sentences.zh: 義康將南，歎曰：「昔謝述唯勸吾退，劉班唯勸吾進；

translations.literal: As Yikang was about to go south, he sighed: "Formerly Xie Shu only urged me to withdraw; Liu Ban only urged me to advance;
translations.idiomatic: As Yikang was about to depart for the south, he sighed, "In the past Xie Shu alone urged me to withdraw, while Liu Ban alone urged me to advance;

sentences.zh: 今班存而述死，其敗也宜哉！」

translations.literal: now Ban lives while Shu is dead—its defeat was fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: now Ban lives while Shu is dead—no wonder ruin came!"

sentences.zh: 上亦曰：「謝述若存，義康必不至此！」。

translations.literal: The emperor also said: "If Xie Shu were alive, Yikang would certainly not have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "If Xie Shu were still alive, Yikang would certainly not have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 以征虜司馬蕭斌為義康咨議參軍，領豫章太守，事無大小，皆以委之。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin, staff officer of the Campaign Against Barbarians, was made Yikang's consulting officer; he was also Inspector of Yuzhang; affairs great and small were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin, staff officer of the campaign against the barbarians, was made Yikang's consulting officer and concurrently inspector of Yuzhang; every matter, great or small, was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 斌，摹之之子也。

translations.literal: Bin was son of Xiao Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was the son of Xiao Mo.

sentences.zh: 使龍驤將軍蕭承之將兵防守。

translations.literal: The Dragon Valiant General Xiao Chengzhi was sent with troops to garrison and defend.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon valiant general Xiao Chengzhi was sent with troops to garrison and guard the region.

sentences.zh: 義康左右愛念者，並聽隨從；

translations.literal: Those among Yikang's attendants who cherished him were all permitted to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Those among Yikang's attendants who were dear to him were all allowed to accompany him;

sentences.zh: 資奉優厚，信賜相系，朝廷大事皆報示之。。

translations.literal: stipends and gifts were generous and unbroken; important court matters were all reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: his stipends and gifts were generous and unceasing, and every important matter of court was reported to him.

sentences.zh: 久之，上就會稽公主宴集，甚歡；

translations.literal: After a long time, the emperor held a banquet with the Princess of Kuaiji; they were very merry;
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, the emperor held a banquet with the Princess of Kuaiji, and they were very merry;

sentences.zh: 主起，再拜叩頭，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: the princess rose, bowed twice, and kowtowed on the ground, grief beyond her own control.
translations.idiomatic: the princess rose, bowed twice, and knocked her forehead to the ground, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 上不曉其意，自起扶之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand her intent and rose himself to support her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not understand her meaning and rose to support her himself.

sentences.zh: 主曰：「車子歲暮必不為陛下所容，今特請其命。」

translations.literal: The princess said: "The carriage at year's end will certainly not be tolerated by Your Majesty—now I specially beg his life."
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "The carriage will certainly not survive the year's end in Your Majesty's court. I beg you now for his life."

sentences.zh: 因慟哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon she wailed bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon she wailed bitterly.

sentences.zh: 上亦流涕，指蔣山曰：「必無此慮。

translations.literal: The emperor also wept, pointed to Mount Jiang and said: "Certainly this worry is unfounded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well, pointed toward Mount Jiang, and said, "You need have no such fear.

sentences.zh: 若違今誓，便是負初寧陵。」

translations.literal: If I break today's oath, that would be betraying Chuning Mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: If I break today's oath, I would be betraying Chuning Mausoleum."

sentences.zh: 即封所飲酒賜義康，並書曰：「會稽姊飲宴憶弟，所餘酒今封送。」

translations.literal: He immediately sealed the wine he had been drinking and sent it to Yikang, with a note: "The Kuaiji elder sister drinks at banquet and thinks of her younger brother; the remaining wine is now sealed and sent."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sealed the wine he had been drinking and sent it to Yikang, with a note that read, "Your elder sister of Kuaiji drank at banquet and thought of her younger brother; the wine that remains is now sealed and sent."

sentences.zh: 故終主之身，義康得無恙。。

translations.literal: Therefore through the princess's lifetime Yikang remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, for as long as the princess lived, Yikang remained unharmed.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：文帝之於義康，友愛之情，其始非不隆也。

translations.literal: Subject Guang says: The emperor Wen's affection toward Yikang at the beginning was certainly not lacking in grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: Emperor Wen's brotherly affection for Yikang at the outset was by no means slight.

sentences.zh: 終於失兄弟之歡，虧君臣之義，跡其亂階，正由劉湛權利之心無有厭已。

translations.literal: In the end he lost the joy of brotherhood and damaged the righteousness of ruler and minister; tracing the steps of the disorder, it was precisely because Liu Zhan's heart for power and profit had no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he lost the joy of brotherhood and damaged the bond between ruler and minister. Tracing the steps of the disorder, it was precisely because Liu Zhan's hunger for power and profit knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「貪人敗類。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "The greedy man ruins his kind."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry says, "The greedy man ruins his kind."

sentences.zh: 其是之謂乎！。

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not what is meant!

sentences.zh: 征南袞州刺史江夏王義恭為司徒、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Inspector of the Campaign South and Yan Province, was made Minister of Works and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and inspector of the campaign south and Yan Province, was made minister of works and recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以臨川王義慶為南袞州刺史，殷景仁為揚州刺史，僕射、吏部尚書如故。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing was made Inspector of Southern Yan Province; Yin Jingren was made Inspector of Yang Province, with Vice Director and Minister of the Civil Office as before.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Liu Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan, was made inspector of Southern Yan Province, and Yin Jingren was made inspector of Yang Province while retaining his titles of vice director and minister of the civil office.

sentences.zh: 義恭懲彭城之敗，雖為總錄，奉行文書而已，上乃安之。

translations.literal: Yigong, chastened by Pengcheng's defeat, though he held overall recording, merely carried out documents—and the emperor was thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Chastened by Pengcheng's fall, Yigong, though he held overall recording, merely carried out documents, and the emperor was thereby reassured.

sentences.zh: 上年給相府錢二千萬，它物稱此；

translations.literal: Each year the emperor granted the ministerial mansion twenty million in cash, other goods in proportion;
translations.idiomatic: Each year the emperor granted the ministerial mansion twenty million in cash, with other goods in proportion;

sentences.zh: 而義恭性奢，用常不足，上又別給錢，年至千萬。。

translations.literal: but Yigong was extravagant by nature and expenditure was constantly insufficient; the emperor additionally gave cash, reaching ten million per year.
translations.idiomatic: but Yigong was extravagant by nature and his expenses were constantly insufficient, so the emperor gave additional cash amounting to ten million each year.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，魏主如山北。。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on dinghai, the Wei emperor went to the region north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, the Wei emperor traveled to the northern mountains.

sentences.zh: 殷景仁既拜揚州，羸疾遂篤，上為之敕西州道上不得有車聲。

translations.literal: Yin Jingren, having received appointment as inspector of Yang Province, grew gravely ill from his wasting disease; the emperor ordered that no sound of carts be allowed on the roads of the western province for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin Jingren took up the Yangzhou inspectorate, his chronic illness grew severe; the emperor decreed that no cart traffic be permitted on western province roads near him.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，卒。

translations.literal: On guichou, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸亥，以光祿大夫王球為僕射。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on guihai, the Palace Attendant Wang Qiu was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guihai, Wang Qiu, palace attendant, was appointed vice director.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以始興王浚為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Prince of Shixing, Jun, was made Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Prince Jun of Shixing was made inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 時浚尚幼，州事悉委後軍長史范曄、主簿沈璞。

translations.literal: At that time Jun was still young; all prefectural affairs were entirely entrusted to the Rear Army Chief of Staff Fan Ye and the Registrar Shen Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was still young, so all Yangzhou business was entrusted to Rear Army chief of staff Fan Ye and registrar Shen Pu.

sentences.zh: 曄，泰之子；

translations.literal: Ye was the son of Tai;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye was Fan Tai's son;

sentences.zh: 璞，林子之子也。

translations.literal: Pu was the son of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pu was Shen Linzi's son.

sentences.zh: 曄尋遷左衛將軍，以吏部郎沈演之為右衛將軍，對掌禁旅；

translations.literal: Ye soon moved to Left Guard General; the Bureau Director Shen Yanzhi was made Right Guard General to jointly command the palace guards;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye was soon transferred to left guard general; Shen Yanzhi, bureau director, was made right guard general, and the two jointly commanded the palace guards;

sentences.zh: 又以庾炳之為吏部郎，俱參機密。

translations.literal: Yu Bingzhi was also made Bureau Director, and all participated in secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bingzhi was also made bureau director; all three shared in confidential counsel.

sentences.zh: 演之，勁之曾孫也。。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was the great-grandson of Jinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi was Shen Jinzhi's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 曄有俊才，而薄情淺行，數犯名教，為士流所鄙。

translations.literal: Ye had brilliant talent, yet shallow feeling and conduct; he repeatedly violated ritual propriety and was despised by the scholar-official class.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye was brilliantly gifted yet cold and shallow in conduct; he repeatedly breached ritual propriety and was scorned by respectable society.

sentences.zh: 性躁競，自謂才用不盡，常怏怏不得志。

translations.literal: Restless and competitive by nature, he felt his talents were not fully employed and was constantly discontent and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Restless and ambitious, he believed his gifts went unused and brooded in perpetual dissatisfaction.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書何尚之言於帝曰：「范曄志趨異常，請出為廣州刺史；

translations.literal: The Minister of the Civil Office He Shangzhi spoke to the emperor, saying: "Fan Ye's ambitions are abnormal—please send him out as Inspector of Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the civil office He Shangzhi told the emperor: "Fan Ye's aims are irregular—send him out as Guangzhou inspector;

sentences.zh: 若在內釁成，不得不加鈇鉞。

translations.literal: if trouble forms within the capital, the axe and halberd cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: if he breeds trouble inside the capital, execution will be unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 鈇鉞亟行，非國家之美也。」

translations.literal: Hasty executions are not beautiful for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Rushing to the axe is no credit to the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「始誅劉湛，復遷范曄，人將謂卿等不能容才，朕信受讒言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Having just executed Liu Zhan, to move Fan Ye again—people will say you cannot tolerate talent; I believe I have accepted slander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "We have only just killed Liu Zhan; to transfer Fan Ye now would make people say you cannot bear talent. I know I have heard slander.

sentences.zh: 但共知其如此，無能為害也。」。

translations.literal: But knowing him thus, he can do no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing him as we do, he cannot harm us."

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏寧南將軍王慧龍卒，呂玄伯留守其墓，終身不去。。

translations.literal: That year the Wei Pacifier of the South Wang Huilong died; Lü Xuanbo guarded his tomb and never left throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei's pacifier of the south Wang Huilong died; Lü Xuanbo kept watch at his tomb and never left it for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 魏主欲以伊□為尚書，封郡公，□辭曰：「尚書務殷，公爵至重，非臣年少愚近所宜膺受。」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor wished to make Yi Bo Minister of the Civil Office and enfeoff him as Duke of a commandery. Bo declined, saying: "The minister's duties are pressing and a ducal rank is weighty—not what one so young, foolish, and of shallow experience should receive."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wished to appoint Yi Bo minister of the civil office and enfeoff him as duke of a commandery. Yi Bo declined: "The ministry is arduous and a ducal title is weighty—unsuited to one as young, crude, and shallow as I am."

sentences.zh: 帝問其所欲，對曰：「中、秘二省多諸文士，若恩矜不已，請參其次。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked what he desired; he replied: "The central and secretariat offices have many literary scholars—if Your Majesty's gracious favor cannot cease, let me serve among them in a lesser post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what post he wanted. He answered: "The central and secretariat bureaus are full of literati; if Your Majesty's kindness will not relent, let me take a lesser place among them."

sentences.zh: 帝善之，以為中護國將軍、秘書監。。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and made him General Who Guards the State within the Center and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed him general who guards the state within the center and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大秦王楊難當復稱武都王。。

translations.literal: The Great King of Qin Yang Nandang again styled himself King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang, great king of Qin, again styled himself king of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之上元嘉十八年（辛巳，公元四四一年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Liu Song, middle reign, upper section—Yuanjia year 18 (xinsi; AD 441).
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 18 of Emperor Wen's reign (xinsi; AD 441).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，魏以沮渠無諱為征西大將軍、涼州牧、酒泉王。。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on guimao, Wei made Juqu Wuhui Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Liang Province, and King of Jiuquan.
