translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guimao, Wei appointed Juqu Wuhui grand general who pacifies the west, governor of Liangzhou, and king of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康至豫章，辭刺史；

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang arrived at Yuzhang and declined the inspectorate;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng reached Yuzhang and declined the inspectorate;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以義康都督江、交、廣三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: on jiachen he was made overseer of military affairs for Jiang, Jiao, and Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: on jiachen he was made overseer of military affairs for Jiang, Jiao, and Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 前龍驤參軍巴東扶令育詣闕上表，稱：「昔袁盎諫漢文帝曰：『淮南王若道路遇霜露死，陛下有殺弟之名。』

translations.literal: The former Dragon-Charger Army aide Fu Lingyu of Badong came to the palace and submitted a memorial, stating: "In former times Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Wen of Han, saying: 'If the King of Huainan should meet his death on the road from cold or dew, Your Majesty will bear the name of having killed a younger brother.'
translations.idiomatic: Former dragon-charger army aide Fu Lingyu of Badong presented a memorial at court, arguing: "Yuan Ang once warned Emperor Wen of Han: 'If the king of Huainan dies on the road from exposure, Your Majesty will be blamed for killing your own brother.'

sentences.zh: 文帝不用，追悔無及。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen did not heed him and later regretted it beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Wen did not listen and later regretted it too late.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康，先朝之愛子，陛下之次弟，若有迷謬之愆，正可數之以善惡，導之以義方，奈何信疑似之嫌，一旦黜削，遠送南垂！

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang is a beloved son of the former reign and Your Majesty's next younger brother; if he has errors born of confusion, one should simply count his good and ill and guide him with moral principle—how can you trust vague suspicions and in a single day demote and banish him, sending him far to the southern marches!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng was a favorite of the late emperor and is Your Majesty's younger brother. If he has stumbled, count his faults and virtues and teach him by moral example—why trust vague suspicion, strip him in a day, and exile him to the far south!

sentences.zh: 草萊黔首，皆為陛下痛之。

translations.literal: Commoners in the grass and brush all ache for Your Majesty on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Common people everywhere grieve for Your Majesty because of this.

sentences.zh: 廬陵往事，足為龜鑒。

translations.literal: The affair of Luling is sufficient as a mirror of tortoise and bronze.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of Luling is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 恐義康年窮命盡，奄忽於南，臣雖微賤，竊為陛下羞之。

translations.literal: I fear that when Yikang's years are spent and his life ends, he may suddenly perish in the south; though I am humble and slight, I secretly feel shame for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Yikang may die in the south before his time; though I am nobody, I am ashamed for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下徒知惡枝之宜伐，豈知伐枝之傷樹！

translations.literal: Your Majesty knows only that evil branches should be cut—do you not know that cutting branches wounds the tree!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sees only that bad branches must be pruned—do you not see that pruning wounds the tree!

sentences.zh: 伏願亟召義康返於京甸，兄弟協和，君臣輯睦，則四海之望塞，多言之路絕矣。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Yikang be swiftly summoned back to the capital region; if brothers are harmonious and ruler and ministers are united, then the hopes of the four seas will be fulfilled and the roads of much talk will be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to recall Yikang quickly to the capital; with brothers reconciled and court united, the realm's hopes will be satisfied and rumor will die.

sentences.zh: 何必司徒公、揚州牧然後可以置彭城王哉！

translations.literal: Why must there be a Minister of Works and an Inspector of Yang Province before the Prince of Pengcheng can be settled!
translations.idiomatic: Must you wait for a minister of works and a Yangzhou inspector before you can restore Prince Pengcheng!

sentences.zh: 若臣所言於國為非，請伏重誅以謝陛下。」

translations.literal: If my words are wrong for the state, I beg to prostrate myself for heavy punishment to answer to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: If I am wrong, let me accept death to answer to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 表奏，即收付建康獄，賜死。。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was immediately taken to the Jiankang prison and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was read; he was seized, sent to Jiankang prison, and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：夫在上為善，若雲行雨施，萬物受其賜；

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: When one above does good, it is like clouds moving and rain spreading—all things receive his bounty;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: When a ruler does good, it is like clouds and rain—every creature shares the gift;

sentences.zh: 及其惡也，若天裂地震，萬物所驚駭，其誰弗知，其誰弗見！

translations.literal: when he does evil, it is like heaven splitting and earth quaking—all things are terrified; who does not know it, who does not see it!
translations.idiomatic: when he turns cruel, it is like heaven rending and earth shaking—every creature is appalled; who does not know, who does not see!

sentences.zh: 豈戮一人之身，鉗一夫之口，所能禳逃，所能弭滅哉？

translations.literal: How can killing one man's body or clamping one man's mouth ward off calamity or extinguish it?
translations.idiomatic: Can slaying one man or silencing one mouth avert or erase such things?

sentences.zh: 是皆不勝其忿怒而有增於疾疹也。

translations.literal: These are all cases of not mastering one's wrath and thereby adding to the sickness.
translations.idiomatic: That is only rage outpacing reason and worsening the disease.

sentences.zh: 以太祖之含弘，尚掩耳於彭城之戮，自斯以後，誰易由言！

translations.literal: Even with the Founding Emperor's magnanimity, he still covered his ears at the execution at Pengcheng; from that time on, who could easily speak freely!
translations.idiomatic: Even the founding emperor's tolerance could not keep him from shutting his ears at Pengcheng; after that, who dared speak plainly!

sentences.zh: 有宋累葉，罕聞直諒，豈骨鯁之氣，俗愧前古？

translations.literal: Through many generations of Song, straight remonstrance was rarely heard—was the bone-in-the-throat spirit of the age ashamed before antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: For generations under Song, honest counsel was rare—had the marrow of integrity shamed the ancients?

sentences.zh: 抑時王刑政使之然乎？

translations.literal: Or was it rather that the times and royal punishments made it so?
translations.idiomatic: Or did the age and its punishments make it so?

sentences.zh: 張約隕於權臣，扶育斃於哲後，宋之鼎鑊，吁，可畏哉！。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue perished at the hands of a powerful minister; Fu Lingyu died at the hands of a wise sovereign—Song's cauldron and chopping block: ah, how dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue fell to a power minister; Fu Lingyu died under a sage ruler—Song's cauldron and axe: how dreadful!

sentences.zh: 魏新興王俊荒淫不法，三月，庚戌，降爵為公。

translations.literal: The Wei Prince of Xinxing Jun was dissolute and lawless; third month, on gengxu, his rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's prince of Xinxing, Jun, was debauched and lawless; in the third month, on gengxu, he was demoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 俊母先得罪死，俊積怨望，有逆謀；

translations.literal: Jun's mother had earlier been condemned and died; Jun nursed resentment and had a treasonous plot;
translations.idiomatic: Jun's mother had already been condemned to death; he brooded on grievance and plotted rebellion;

sentences.zh: 事覺，賜死。

translations.literal: when the affair was discovered, he was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: when the plot was exposed, he was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏賜郁久閭乞列歸爵為朔方王，沮渠萬年為張掖王。。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Wei enfeoffed the Rouran Qiliegui as King of Shuofang and Juqu Wannian as King of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Wei enfeoffed the Rouran Qiliegui as king of Shuofang and Juqu Wannian as king of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，沮渠唐兒叛沮渠無諱；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Juqu Tang'er rebelled against Juqu Wuhui;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Juqu Tang'er rebelled against Juqu Wuhui;

sentences.zh: 無諱留從弟天周守酒泉，與弟宜得引兵擊唐兒，唐兒敗死。

translations.literal: Wuhui left his younger cousin Tian Zhou to hold Jiuquan and, with his brother Yide, led troops to attack Tang'er; Tang'er was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui left his cousin Tian Zhou to hold Jiuquan and marched with his brother Yide against Tang'er; Tang'er was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 魏以無諱終為邊患，庚辰，遣鎮南將軍奚眷擊酒泉。。

translations.literal: Wei judged that Wuhui would ultimately be a border trouble; on gengchen they sent the Pacifier of the South Xi Juan to attack Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Wuhui would remain a frontier menace, on gengchen Wei sent pacifier of the south Xi Juan against Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，辛亥，魏遣散騎侍郎張偉來聘。。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on xinhai, Wei sent the Gentleman of the Loose Retinue Zhang Wei on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on xinhai, Wei sent gentleman of the loose retinue Zhang Wei as envoy.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊戌，魏永昌王健卒。。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on wuxu, the Wei Prince of Yongchang Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuxu, Wei's prince of Yongchang, Jian, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，戊子，王球卒。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on wuzi, Wang Qiu died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on wuzi, Wang Qiu died.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以丹陽尹孟顗為尚書僕射。。

translations.literal: On jihai, Meng Yun, Governor of Danyang, was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Meng Yun, governor of Danyang, was appointed vice director.

sentences.zh: 酒泉城中食盡，萬餘口皆餓死，沮渠天周殺妻以食戰士。

translations.literal: Food in Jiuquan city was exhausted; more than ten thousand people all starved to death; Juqu Tian Zhou killed his wife to feed the fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuquan ran out of food, more than ten thousand people starved; Juqu Tian Zhou killed his wife to feed his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏奚眷拔酒泉，獲天周，送平城，殺之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Wei general Xi Juan took Jiuquan, captured Tian Zhou, sent him to Pingcheng, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Xi Juan stormed Jiuquan, seized Tian Zhou, sent him to Pingcheng, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 沮渠無諱乏食，且畏魏兵之盛，乃謀西度流沙，遣其弟安周西擊郪善。

translations.literal: Juqu Wuhui lacked food and also feared the strength of Wei troops; he therefore planned to cross the drifting sands westward and sent his younger brother An Zhou west to attack Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Short of food and fearing Wei's armies, Juqu Wuhui planned to cross the western desert and sent his brother An Zhou west against Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 郪善王欲降，會魏使者至，勸令拒守；

translations.literal: The king of Shanshan wished to surrender, but a Wei envoy arrived and urged him to hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: The Shanshan king was ready to submit, but a Wei envoy arrived and persuaded him to resist;

sentences.zh: 安周不能克，退何東城。。

translations.literal: An Zhou could not overcome them and withdrew to Hedong Fort.
translations.idiomatic: An Zhou failed to take the city and retreated to Hedong Fort.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊難當傾國入寇，謀據蜀土，遣其建忠將軍苻衝出東洛以御梁州兵；

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Nandang led his whole state in invasion, plotting to seize Shu territory; he sent his General Who Establishes Loyalty Fu Chong out from Dongluo to oppose the Liang Province troops;
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Yang Nandang invaded at full strength, aiming to seize Shu; he sent general who establishes loyalty Fu Chong from Dongluo to block Liangzhou forces;

sentences.zh: 梁、秦二州刺史劉真道擊沖，斬之。

translations.literal: the Inspectors of Liang and Qin Provinces Liu Zhendao attacked Chong and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Qin inspectors Liu Zhendao attacked Chong and killed him.

sentences.zh: 真道，懷敬之子也。

translations.literal: Zhendao was the son of Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhendao was Liu Huaijing's son.

sentences.zh: 難當攻拔葭萌，獲晉壽太守申坦，遂圍涪城。

translations.literal: Nandang attacked and took Jiameng, captured the Jinshou Prefect Shen Tan, and then besieged Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang took Jiameng, captured Jinshou prefect Shen Tan, and besieged Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 巴西、梓潼二郡太守劉道錫嬰城固守，難當攻之十餘日，不克，乃還。

translations.literal: The Prefects of Baxi and Zitong Liu Daoxi held the cities firm and defended; Nandang attacked for more than ten days without overcoming them and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Baxi and Zitong prefect Liu Daoxi held his cities; after ten days of assault Nandang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道錫，道產之弟也。

translations.literal: Daoxi was the younger brother of Daochan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxi was Liu Daochan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸亥，詔龍驤將軍裴方明等帥甲士三千人，又發荊、雍二州兵以討難當，皆受劉真道節度。。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on guihai, an edict ordered the Dragon-Charger General Pei Fangming and others to command three thousand armored soldiers, and also to mobilize troops from Jing and Yong provinces to punish Nandang—all under Liu Zhendao's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guihai, the court ordered dragon-charger general Pei Fangming and others to lead three thousand armored men, with additional troops from Jing and Yong, to campaign against Nandang—all under Liu Zhendao.

sentences.zh: 晉寧太守爨松子反，寧州刺史徐循討平之。。

translations.literal: The Jinning Prefect Cuan Songzi rebelled; the Jinzhou Inspector Xu Xun attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinning prefect Cuan Songzi rebelled; Jinzhou inspector Xu Xun suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 天門蠻田向求等反，破漊中；

translations.literal: The Tianmen barbarians Tian Xiangqiu and others rebelled and broke Louzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Tianmen barbarians Tian Xiangqiu and others rebelled and raided Louzhong;

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史衡陽王義季遣行參軍曹孫念討破之。。

translations.literal: the Jing Province Inspector, the Prince of Hengyang Yiji, sent the Acting Aide Cao Sunnian to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector Prince Yiji of Hengyang sent acting aide Cao Sunnian, who defeated them.

sentences.zh: 魏寇謙之言於魏主曰：「今陛下以真君御世，建靜輪天宮之法，開古以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Kou Qianzhi spoke to the Wei emperor, saying: "Now Your Majesty rules the age as the Perfected Lord and has established the law of the Still-Wheel Heavenly Palace—since antiquity opened, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Qianzhi told the Wei emperor: "Your Majesty reigns as the Perfected Lord and has founded the Still-Wheel Heavenly Palace rite—nothing like it since the world began.

sentences.zh: 應登受符書，以彰聖德。」

translations.literal: You should ascend and receive the talisman writ to display sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: You should receive the talisman writ and proclaim your sacred virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.
